This testplan turns every requirement of the CHERIoT memory subsystem (`cheriot_mem_sys`) into
testpoints for formal property verification (FPV). It sits in five files: this one says how to read
a testpoint and maps every testpoint to its block; the xref:{tp1}#checker1[checker 1 testplan] (tag path),
the xref:{tp2}#checker2[checker 2 testplan] (meta access) and the xref:{tp3}#checker3[checker 3 testplan]
(revocation engine) hold the testpoints of each checker; the xref:{tps}#subsystem_part[subsystem-wide testplan]
holds the shared terms, the subsystem-wide and end-to-end testpoints, the run variants and the open
items. Each of those four files is included below, so this file shows the whole
testplan; edit the four files, never the sections assembled here. The requirements, the assumptions and the questions for the designers are in the
requirements doc; the three checkers that run the testpoints, with their
environments and contracts, are in the xref:../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc[TB
architecture].

== Overview

[[how_to_read]]
=== How to read this testplan

FPV runs no tests: the tool tries every input sequence the environment allows. A testpoint
therefore states the rule, the checks that decide it and the cases the tool must be shown to reach.
A software testplan picks configurations and checks the result; this testplan keeps its method and
changes its form:

[cols="3,5",options="header"]
|===
|In a software testplan |In this FPV testplan

|Choose a configuration, run it, observe |The tool tries every configuration at once. A cover shows
that the configuration you care about is reached
|Vary one parameter, hold the rest |One cover per value of that parameter, the others held: the
*Cases* table of a testpoint
|Exercise the full truth table of the conditions |One cover per row; one assertion of the rule
checks every row at once: the *Truth table*
|Randomise values |Free inputs: the tool tries every value, not a sample
|Expected result |The rule's result, in the *Rule* line, checked by an assertion in both directions
|Edge cases, with steps |Covers on boundary values (*Edge cases*); the assertion already checks them
|"Not directly observable" |Often observable here: the checks sit on the subsystem's ports, e.g.
every read the engine makes on `tbre_tl_h`
|===

Every testpoint, in all four testpoint files, has these parts; a part with nothing to say is left
out:

[cols="1,5",options="header"]
|===
|Part |Holds

|Rule |The behaviour the testpoint checks, in plain words.
|Observed at |The ports where the checks look.
|Checks |Each assertion once: its ID, its name, its kind and exactly what it asserts. The ID,
`CHK_<TESTPOINT>_<NN>`, never changes; the TB architecture maps each ID to the property that
implements it.
|Requirements |Every requirement of the testpoint, the check that proves it, and why that check is
enough.
|Follows from |For a testpoint closed by composition, in place of Checks, Cases and Run: the
requirements of the checkers and the premises it follows from.
|Cases |Covers the tool must reach, one input varied at a time, each with its expected result.
|Truth table |One cover per row of the rule's conditions.
|Edge cases |Covers on boundary values: first and last of a range, seams, events in one cycle.
|Never |What must never happen.
|Run |The environment of the run that checks it.
|Blocked by |The open questions an expected value waits on.
|===

[cols="1,5",options="header"]
|===
|Kind of check |Meaning

|forward |Whenever the rule says the design must act, it acts: stimulus implies response.
|backward |The design acts only when the rule says so: response implies stimulus. A one-bit credit,
set by the stimulus and used up by the response, catches a response with no stimulus and a second
response to one stimulus.
|safety |A signal holds a value in every cycle.
|liveness |Something happens in the end, with no bound on when.
|cover |A case the tool must show is reachable. An unreachable cover means every check of that case
proves nothing: it is vacuous.
|===

In running text a check or case name is in italics, after its testpoint when it belongs to another
one: `tf_forward` _no extra host request_. Wherever a check is named, its ID follows as a link.

Every check holds in run V1, the main environment of the TB architecture, unless its Run line
says otherwise (xref:{tps}#run_variants[run variants]).

* Every expected value comes from a rule and its spec citation, never from the RTL. Numbers in
  examples are Earl Grey's, computed with a script from the rules. The proofs bind the design with
  Earl Grey's parameters (TB architecture, How the checkers are built), so every result holds for
  that configuration; another configuration reruns the same testplan with its values.
* An assertion holds for every legal input; the covers prove that the inputs that matter are among
  them. Both are needed: an assertion without its covers can pass because nothing happened.

== Checker 1: tag path


=== Terms

[cols="2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Term |Meaning

|Needs a lookup |A core request needs a meta request when it is, in CHERIoT mode and to a tagged
region, a 64-bit-aligned read hinted as a capability load, or a write, and is not a capability
store to the NVM (`REQ_TF_02a`, `REQ_TF_03a`).
|Tag word, tag bit |The meta word that holds an address's tag, and the bit within it: for the main
SRAM, word `0x1100_8C00` + 4 × (offset / 256), bit (offset / 8) % 32, with offset the address
minus `0x1000_0000`; for the NVM the same from `0x1100_0C00` and `0x3000_0000`. The bit order is
question an open question.
|Matched |A word of a capability store to the NVM whose NVM read succeeded, that is a full-word
`PutFullData` in sequence, and whose data and data integrity equal the NVM's.
|Faulty word |A word of a capability store to the NVM that is out of sequence, partial, carries a
bad command or data integrity, or gets an NVM answer with a bad response integrity.
|Owed tag write |From the cycle W1's NVM answer arrives, when W0 and W1 both matched, until the
meta port takes the tag write.
|Operation |A request the RMW filter accepted, until its answer is taken. Its requests to the meta
SRAM are its `Get` and, for a write whose bit changes, its write-back.
|Faulty `Get` answer |The answer to a write's `Get` with no `d_error` but a broken response or data
integrity. The spec only raises the alert for it, so the RMW filter checks claim nothing about
what the filter does for that write afterwards (question an open question).
|===

=== Tag filter

How the tag filter works: xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc#_tag_filter[design
architecture doc, Tag filter].

.Testpoints of the tag filter
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_tf_forward,tf_forward>> |Every core access reaches the host port once, unchanged, in the cycle the core presents it; its answer carries the host answer's fields when its last part arrives.
|<<tp_tf_lookup,tf_lookup>> |A request that needs a tag issues exactly one meta request, in the same cycle; every other request issues none.
|<<tp_tf_meta_request,tf_meta_request>> |Each meta request names the right tag word and bit, and a write asks for the tag its sideband carries.
|<<tp_tf_sticky_tag,tf_sticky_tag>> |The tag returned with each answer: W0 of a capability load gets the meta tag, the W1 after it the captured copy, every other answer 0.
|<<tp_tf_errors,tf_errors>> |An error in the host or the meta answer reaches the core, no error is invented, and a merged error keeps the integrity valid or broken as it was.
|<<tp_tf_flow,tf_flow>> |Meta answers are always taken, and every request is accepted and answered exactly once.
|===

[[tp_tf_forward]]
==== tf_forward: every access forwarded once, unchanged, with its answer

*Rule:* every core request appears once on the host port, with every field unchanged, in the cycle
the core presents it. Its answer to the core carries the host answer's fields, in the cycle its
last part arrives.

*Observed at:* the core port `cored_tl_d` and the host port `cored_tl_h`, both channels.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tf_forward_01]]`CHK_TF_FORWARD_01` |forwarded unchanged |forward |A request presented by the core and not yet forwarded is presented
on the host port in the same cycle, with the same address, opcode, size, mask, data, `a_source` and
`a_user`.
|[[chk_tf_forward_02]]`CHK_TF_FORWARD_02` |no extra host request |backward |A request presented on the host port belongs to a core request
presented and not yet forwarded.
|[[chk_tf_forward_03]]`CHK_TF_FORWARD_03` |accepted after forwarded |forward |A core request is accepted only once its host request has been
taken, in that cycle or before.
|[[chk_tf_forward_04]]`CHK_TF_FORWARD_04` |answer has host fields |forward |An answer to the core carries the host answer's `d_opcode`,
`d_size`, `d_source`, `d_data` and data integrity, and its response integrity when no meta error is
merged in.
|[[chk_tf_forward_05]]`CHK_TF_FORWARD_05` |answer on last part |forward |An answer is presented to the core in the cycle its last part (the host answer, and the meta answer if a lookup was made) arrives, and not before.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Every access forwarded (`REQ_TF_01a`) |_accepted after forwarded_ (<<chk_tf_forward_03,CHK_TF_FORWARD_03>>)
|The core only lets go of a request once it is accepted, and acceptance needs the host request to
have been taken first. So no accepted request can skip the host port.

|No access forwarded twice (`REQ_TF_01d`) |_no extra host request_ (<<chk_tf_forward_02,CHK_TF_FORWARD_02>>)
|Each core request gives one credit, and its first host request uses it up. A second host request
for the same core request finds no credit and fails the check.

|No request invented (`REQ_TF_01c`) |_no extra host request_ (<<chk_tf_forward_02,CHK_TF_FORWARD_02>>)
|A host request with no core request behind it finds no credit and fails the check. It is checked
when presented, not only when accepted, which also catches a request the host port never takes.

|Address unchanged (`REQ_TF_01b`) |_forwarded unchanged_ (<<chk_tf_forward_01,CHK_TF_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the host request's address with the core request's in the cycle it is
forwarded. Any changed bit fails it.

|Opcode unchanged (`REQ_TF_01e`) |_forwarded unchanged_ (<<chk_tf_forward_01,CHK_TF_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the host request's opcode with the core request's in the cycle it is
forwarded. A read turned into a write, or the reverse, fails it.

|Size unchanged (`REQ_TF_01f`) |_forwarded unchanged_ (<<chk_tf_forward_01,CHK_TF_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the host request's size with the core request's. A changed size fails it.

|Byte mask unchanged (`REQ_TF_01g`) |_forwarded unchanged_ (<<chk_tf_forward_01,CHK_TF_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the host request's mask with the core request's. A byte added to or dropped
from a store fails it.

|Data unchanged (`REQ_TF_01h`) |_forwarded unchanged_ (<<chk_tf_forward_01,CHK_TF_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the host request's data with the core request's. Any changed data bit fails
it.

|Source ID unchanged (`REQ_TF_01i`) |_forwarded unchanged_ (<<chk_tf_forward_01,CHK_TF_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the host request's `a_source` with the core request's. A changed ID fails it.

|User bits unchanged (`REQ_TF_01j`) |_forwarded unchanged_ (<<chk_tf_forward_01,CHK_TF_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the host request's `a_user`, its integrity included, with the core request's.
Any changed bit fails it.

|Answer's opcode (`REQ_TF_07a`) |_answer has host fields_ (<<chk_tf_forward_04,CHK_TF_FORWARD_04>>)
|The check compares the answer's `d_opcode` with that of the host answer it joins. A changed opcode
fails it.

|Answer's size (`REQ_TF_07b`) |_answer has host fields_ (<<chk_tf_forward_04,CHK_TF_FORWARD_04>>)
|The check compares the answer's `d_size` with the host answer's. A changed size fails it.

|Answer's source ID (`REQ_TF_07c`) |_answer has host fields_ (<<chk_tf_forward_04,CHK_TF_FORWARD_04>>)
|The check compares the answer's `d_source` with the host answer's. An answer joined to the wrong
host answer, or with a changed ID, fails it.

|Answer's data (`REQ_TF_07d`) |_answer has host fields_ (<<chk_tf_forward_04,CHK_TF_FORWARD_04>>)
|The check compares the answer's `d_data` with the host answer's. Another request's data fails it.

|Answer's data integrity (`REQ_TF_07e`) |_answer has host fields_ (<<chk_tf_forward_04,CHK_TF_FORWARD_04>>)
|The check compares the answer's data integrity with the host answer's. Any change fails it.

|Answer's response integrity (`REQ_TF_07f`) |_answer has host fields_ (<<chk_tf_forward_04,CHK_TF_FORWARD_04>>)
|With no meta error merged in, the check compares the answer's response integrity with the host
answer's. With a meta error, `tf_errors` checks it.

|Request at the host port in the same cycle (`REQ_TF_16a`) |_forwarded unchanged_ (<<chk_tf_forward_01,CHK_TF_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check requires the host request in the very cycle the core presents it. One cycle late fails
it.

|Answer in the cycle its last part arrives (`REQ_TF_16b`) |_answer on last part_ (<<chk_tf_forward_05,CHK_TF_FORWARD_05>>)
|The check requires the answer in the cycle the last part arrives, and no earlier. Early or one
cycle late fails it.
|===

.Cases
[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Request or timing

|Get to SRAM |`Get` of the main SRAM, not hinted
|plain store to NVM |`PutFullData` to the NVM with tag 0
|byte store to SRAM |`PutPartialData` of one byte to the main SRAM
|Get to peripheral |`Get` of a peripheral, outside both tagged regions
|W1 while W0 open |two requests outstanding: W0 and W1 of a capability load
|host port stalls |the host port stalls (`a_ready` = 0) while the meta port takes the lookup
|meta port stalls |the meta port stalls while the host port takes the request
|meta answer first |an answer whose meta part arrives before its host part
|host answer first |an answer whose host part arrives before its meta part
|both parts together |an answer whose meta and host parts arrive in one cycle
|===

*Edge cases:* _host answer error_, the host answers with `d_error`; _back to back_, requests in
consecutive cycles; _request in answer cycle_, the second request presented in the cycle the first
is answered.

*Never:* a request on the host port the core did not present; a second one for the same core
request; a core request accepted but never forwarded; a changed field; an answer before its last
part arrived, or one cycle after.

*Run:* V1. Capability stores to the NVM are left out: their host request is a `Get`
(<<tp_wtrc_store>>).

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for _no extra host request_: the check takes the core
to hold its request until it is accepted.

'''

[[tp_tf_lookup]]
==== tf_lookup: when a tag is looked up

*Rule:* a core request that needs a lookup issues exactly one meta request, in the cycle the core
presents it. Every other request issues none.

*Observed at:* the core port and the tag filter's meta port (input 0 of the 2:1 tag arbiter).

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tf_lookup_01]]`CHK_TF_LOOKUP_01` |lookup in same cycle |forward |A request presented that needs a lookup, whose lookup is not yet
taken, has its meta request presented in the same cycle.
|[[chk_tf_lookup_02]]`CHK_TF_LOOKUP_02` |no unneeded lookup |backward |A meta request presented belongs to a request presented that needs a
lookup and whose lookup is not yet taken.
|[[chk_tf_lookup_03]]`CHK_TF_LOOKUP_03` |lookup carries valid integrity |forward |Every meta request presented carries a valid command
integrity.
|===

Both lookup checks hold while no WTRC tag write is owed: an owed tag write goes to the meta port
ahead of any lookup.

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Hinted aligned read is looked up (`REQ_TF_02a`) |_lookup in same cycle_ (<<chk_tf_lookup_01,CHK_TF_LOOKUP_01>>)
|For every request that needs a lookup, the check requires its meta request. A hinted aligned
read to a tagged region in CHERIoT mode is one, so a missing lookup fails it.

|At most one lookup for that read (`REQ_TF_02b`) |_no unneeded lookup_ (<<chk_tf_lookup_02,CHK_TF_LOOKUP_02>>)
|The request's credit is used up by its first meta request, so a second one fails the check.

|Write is looked up (`REQ_TF_03a`) |_lookup in same cycle_ (<<chk_tf_lookup_01,CHK_TF_LOOKUP_01>>)
|A write to a tagged region in CHERIoT mode needs a lookup, so the check requires its meta request.

|At most one lookup for that write (`REQ_TF_03b`) |_no unneeded lookup_ (<<chk_tf_lookup_02,CHK_TF_LOOKUP_02>>)
|The same credit as for the read catches a second meta request.

|No lookup in ePMP mode (`REQ_TF_04a`) |_no unneeded lookup_ (<<chk_tf_lookup_02,CHK_TF_LOOKUP_02>>)
|In ePMP mode no request needs a lookup, so any meta request finds no credit and fails the check.
The cases try all 15 ePMP values of the mode enable.

|No other lookup in CHERIoT mode (`REQ_TF_04b`) |_no unneeded lookup_ (<<chk_tf_lookup_02,CHK_TF_LOOKUP_02>>)
|A plain read, a W1 read or an access outside the tagged regions gives no credit, so its meta
request fails the check.

|Lookup in the same cycle (`REQ_TF_16c`) |_lookup in same cycle_ (<<chk_tf_lookup_01,CHK_TF_LOOKUP_01>>)
|The check requires the meta request in the very cycle the core presents the request.

|Lookup has a valid integrity (`REQ_TF_17`) |_lookup carries valid integrity_ (<<chk_tf_lookup_03,CHK_TF_LOOKUP_03>>)
|The check recomputes the command integrity of every meta request. Nothing else checks it: the
TL-UL bus checker leaves every integrity field free.
|===

.Cases: one input varied from the base case, a hinted W0 `Get`
[cols="2,2,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Varied |Request |Lookup

|hinted W0 Get |none: the base case |CHERIoT mode, `Get` `0x1000_1238`, hinted |1
|hinted W1 Get |address bit 2 |`Get` `0x1000_123C`, hinted (W1) |0
|unhinted Get |hint |`Get` `0x1000_1238`, not hinted |0
|word store |opcode |`PutFullData` `0x1000_1238`, tag 0 (`sw`) |1
|byte store |opcode |`PutPartialData` `0x1000_1239`, tag 0 (`sb`) |1
|capability store |opcode, tag |`PutFullData` `0x1000_1238`, tag 1 (`csc`) |1
|NVM capability load |region |`Get` `0x3000_0400`, hinted |1
|NVM capability store |region, opcode |`PutFullData` `0x3000_0400`, tag 1 |0
|NVM word store |region, opcode |`PutFullData` `0x3000_0400`, tag 0 |1
|peripheral Get |region |`Get` `0x4000_0000` (a peripheral), hinted |0
|bitmap store |region |`PutFullData` `0x1100_0100` (the bitmap window), tag 0 |0
|ePMP mode |mode |mode enable `MuBi4False` |0
|invalid mode |mode |mode enable `4'h0`, an invalid encoding |0
|===

.Truth table: one cover per cell
[cols="3,2,2,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Access |CHERIoT mode, main SRAM |CHERIoT mode, NVM |CHERIoT mode, other address |ePMP mode
(15 values)

|`Get`, hinted, W0 |1 |1 |0 |0
|`Get`, hinted, W1 |0 |0 |0 |0
|`Get`, not hinted |0 |0 |0 |0
|write, tag 0 |1 |1 |0 |0
|write, tag 1 |1 |0: WTRC |0 |0
|===

*Edge cases:* _region edge address_, one cover each for the first and last capability of each
region and one beyond: `0x0FFF_FFF8` (0), `0x1000_0000` (1), `0x1002_FFF8` (1), `0x1003_0000` (0),
`0x2FFF_FFF8` (0), `0x3000_0000` (1), `0x301F_FFF8` (1), `0x3020_0000` (0); both sides of the seam,
`0x1001_FFF8` and `0x1002_0000` (both 1). _Every mode value_: one cover for each of the 16 values
of the mode enable.

*Never:* a lookup in ePMP mode; for a W1 load, a plain load, a peripheral, the bitmap window, or a
capability store to the NVM; two lookups for one request.

*Run:* V1.

[[tp_tf_meta_request]]
==== tf_meta_request: which word, which bit, which tag

*Rule:* a meta request addresses the tag word of the request's address, with the tag bit as its
bit select. A read's meta request is a `Get`; a write's is a write carrying the write's tag
sideband as the tag to write.

*Observed at:* the tag filter's meta port.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tf_meta_request_01]]`CHK_TF_META_REQUEST_01` |tag word and bit |forward |Every meta request has the tag word of its request's address as its
address and the tag bit as its bit select.
|[[chk_tf_meta_request_02]]`CHK_TF_META_REQUEST_02` |write carries its tag |forward |A write's meta request carries the write's tag sideband as the tag
to write.
|[[chk_tf_meta_request_03]]`CHK_TF_META_REQUEST_03` |Get only for a read |forward |A read's meta request is a `Get`; a write's is not.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|The right meta word (`REQ_TF_05a`) |_tag word and bit_ (<<chk_tf_meta_request_01,CHK_TF_META_REQUEST_01>>)
|The check computes the tag word from the request's address and compares it with the meta
request's address. Another word fails it.

|The right bit (`REQ_TF_05b`) |_tag word and bit_ (<<chk_tf_meta_request_01,CHK_TF_META_REQUEST_01>>)
|The check computes the tag bit from the address and compares it with the bit select. A
neighbour's bit fails it.

|Plain store asks for tag 0 (`REQ_TF_06a`) |_write carries its tag_ (<<chk_tf_meta_request_02,CHK_TF_META_REQUEST_02>>), _Get only for a read_ (<<chk_tf_meta_request_03,CHK_TF_META_REQUEST_03>>)
|The first check compares the tag to write with the sideband, 0 for a plain store. The second makes
sure the meta request is a write at all, so the RMW filter really writes the 0.

|Capability store asks for tag 1 (`REQ_TF_06b`) |_write carries its tag_ (<<chk_tf_meta_request_02,CHK_TF_META_REQUEST_02>>), _Get only for a read_ (<<chk_tf_meta_request_03,CHK_TF_META_REQUEST_03>>)
|The same two checks, with the sideband 1 of a capability store.
|===

.Cases: address to meta word and bit (bit order of question an open question)
[cols="2,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Request address |Meta word, bit select

|W0, bit 7 |`0x1000_1238` (W0 load or store) |`0x1100_8C48`, 7
|W1, bit 7 |`0x1000_123C` (store to W1) |`0x1100_8C48`, 7
|byte in capability |`0x1000_1239` to `0x1000_123F` (byte stores) |`0x1100_8C48`, 7
|next capability, bit 8 |`0x1000_1240` |`0x1100_8C48`, 8
|first SRAM capability |`0x1000_0000` |`0x1100_8C00`, 0
|seam |`0x1001_FFF8`, `0x1002_0000` |`0x1100_93FC`, 31; `0x1100_9400`, 0
|last SRAM capability |`0x1002_FFF8` |`0x1100_97FC`, 31
|NVM capabilities |`0x3000_0000`, `0x3000_0400`, `0x301F_FFF8` |`0x1100_0C00`, 0; `0x1100_0C10`,
0; `0x1100_8BFC`, 31
|===

.Cases: tag to write
[cols="2,4,1",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Write |Tag

|plain store, tag 0 |`sw`, `sh`, `sb` over a capability |0
|capability store, tag 1 |`csc` of a tagged capability, both words |1
|capability store, tag 0 |`csc` of an untagged capability |0
|===

*Never:* a meta address outside `0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF`; another capability's bit select; tag
1 for a plain store.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, the bit order of the tag bit.

'''

[[tp_tf_sticky_tag]]
==== tf_sticky_tag: the tag returned with each answer

*Rule:* the tag returned with each answer to the core is:

* 0 for a write; a write's answer leaves the captured tag unchanged;
* the meta answer's tag for W0 of a capability load, which is also captured;
* the captured tag for the W1 that follows, after which the capture is cleared;
* 0 for every other read.

The capture is 0 after reset. A plain read answered between W0 and W1 is left open by the spec; the
core never sends one, so the testplan claims nothing for it
(xref:{tp}#not_covered[not covered]).

*Observed at:* the tag returned to the core (`cored_tag_d2h`) with the answers on the core port.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tf_sticky_tag_01]]`CHK_TF_STICKY_TAG_01` |answer tag follows rule |forward |The tag of every answer to the core equals the rule's value. The
tag of an answer with `d_error` is not checked, but W0's tag is still captured.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|W0 gets its meta answer's tag (`REQ_TF_08`) |_answer tag follows rule_ (<<chk_tf_sticky_tag_01,CHK_TF_STICKY_TAG_01>>)
|For W0 of a capability load without `d_error`, the rule's value is the meta answer's tag. Any
other tag fails the check.

|W1 gets the captured tag (`REQ_TF_09`) |_answer tag follows rule_ (<<chk_tf_sticky_tag_01,CHK_TF_STICKY_TAG_01>>)
|For the W1 after a W0, the rule's value is the captured tag. A W1 that loses or changes it fails.

|Capture cleared after W1 (`REQ_TF_10`) |_answer tag follows rule_ (<<chk_tf_sticky_tag_01,CHK_TF_STICKY_TAG_01>>)
|The case _upper word after load_ reads the upper word again with a plain load right after the
capability load. The rule expects 0; a capture not cleared would return 1 and fail.

|Write answer untagged (`REQ_TF_11a`) |_answer tag follows rule_ (<<chk_tf_sticky_tag_01,CHK_TF_STICKY_TAG_01>>)
|For a write, the rule's value is 0. A tagged write answer fails the check.

|Write answer leaves the capture alone (`REQ_TF_11b`) |_answer tag follows rule_ (<<chk_tf_sticky_tag_01,CHK_TF_STICKY_TAG_01>>)
|A write answered between W0 and W1 must not change the tag W1 gets. On the core's tag filter the
case cannot happen: the core sends W1 right after W0. On the engine's tag filter it can, when the
engine clears a tag, and the same check decides it there (checker 3).

|Other reads untagged (`REQ_TF_11c`) |_answer tag follows rule_ (<<chk_tf_sticky_tag_01,CHK_TF_STICKY_TAG_01>>)
|For a plain load, a load outside the tagged regions or a load in ePMP mode, the rule's value is 0.
A tag of 1 fails the check.
|===

.Cases
[cols="2,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Access |Tags returned

|SRAM capability, tag 1 |`clc` from the main SRAM, stored tag 1 |1, 1
|SRAM capability, tag 0 |`clc` from the main SRAM, stored tag 0 |0, 0
|NVM capability, tag 1 |`clc` from the NVM, stored tag 1 |1, 1
|word load |`lw` of a tagged capability's word |0
|load in ePMP mode |`clc` in ePMP mode |0, 0
|peripheral load |`clc` of a peripheral address |0, 0
|store answer |a store's answer |0
|W0 error, then W1 |`clc` whose W0 answer has `d_error` |not checked, then the capture
|upper word after load |a plain `lw` of `c + 4` right after a `clc` of `c` with stored tag 1 |0
|===

*Never:* tag 1 on a write answer, on a plain load, on a load outside the tagged regions or in ePMP
mode; a capture still returned after its W1.

*Run:* V1.

'''

[[tp_tf_errors]]
==== tf_errors: errors and response integrity

*Rule:* `d_error` towards the core is set when the host answer has an error, or when a lookup was
made and the meta answer has one, and is clear otherwise. When only the meta answer has an error,
the response integrity stays valid if the host's was valid and broken if it was broken.

*Observed at:* the answers on the core port, the host answers on the host port, the meta answers
at the meta port.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tf_errors_01]]`CHK_TF_ERRORS_01` |error when a part has one |forward |An answer whose host answer or joined meta answer has an
error has `d_error`.
|[[chk_tf_errors_02]]`CHK_TF_ERRORS_02` |no error without a cause |backward |An answer with `d_error` has a host answer or a joined meta
answer with an error.
|[[chk_tf_errors_03]]`CHK_TF_ERRORS_03` |merged error keeps integrity |forward |When only the meta answer has an error, the answer's
response integrity is valid exactly when the host answer's was.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Host error reaches the core (`REQ_TF_12a`) |_error when a part has one_ (<<chk_tf_errors_01,CHK_TF_ERRORS_01>>)
|Whenever the host answer has `d_error`, the check requires it on the answer. A lost error fails.

|Meta error reaches the core (`REQ_TF_12c`) |_error when a part has one_ (<<chk_tf_errors_01,CHK_TF_ERRORS_01>>)
|Whenever the joined meta answer has an error, the check requires `d_error`. A lost tag error
fails.

|No error without a cause (`REQ_TF_12b`) |_no error without a cause_ (<<chk_tf_errors_02,CHK_TF_ERRORS_02>>)
|An answer with `d_error` and no error in either part fails the check.

|Valid integrity stays valid (`REQ_TF_13a`) |_merged error keeps integrity_ (<<chk_tf_errors_03,CHK_TF_ERRORS_03>>)
|With the host integrity valid and only a meta error, the check requires a valid response
integrity. A valid answer made to look corrupt fails.

|Broken integrity stays broken (`REQ_TF_13b`) |_merged error keeps integrity_ (<<chk_tf_errors_03,CHK_TF_ERRORS_03>>)
|With the host integrity broken, the check requires it still broken. A corrupt answer made to look
valid fails.
|===

.Truth table: one cover per row, for a read and for a write
[cols="1,1,1,1,3",options="header"]
|===
|Host error |Lookup |Meta error |`d_error` |Response integrity

|0 |0 |- |0 |the host's
|1 |0 |- |1 |the host's
|0 |1 |0 |0 |the host's
|0 |1 |1 |1 |adjusted: valid if and only if the host's was valid (two covers: host integrity valid, broken)
|1 |1 |0 |1 |the host's
|1 |1 |1 |1 |the host's
|===

*Never:* an error lost; an error invented; a broken integrity made valid; a valid integrity made
broken.

*Run:* V1. Broken integrities are legal stimulus: integrity is free on every port.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, the integrity code.

'''

[[tp_tf_flow]]
==== tf_flow: no stall, no lost answer

*Rule:* the meta port takes every meta answer it is offered. Every request is accepted and answered
exactly once, given the host and meta ports accept and answer.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tf_flow_01]]`CHK_TF_FLOW_01` |meta answer taken |safety |The meta port's `d_ready` is 1 in every cycle a meta answer is offered.
|[[chk_tf_flow_02]]`CHK_TF_FLOW_02` |no extra answer |backward |No request is answered twice: one credit per accepted request.
|[[chk_tf_flow_03]]`CHK_TF_FLOW_03` |request eventually accepted |liveness |Every request presented is accepted in the end.
|[[chk_tf_flow_04]]`CHK_TF_FLOW_04` |request eventually answered |liveness |Every accepted request is answered in the end.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Meta answers always taken (`REQ_TF_14`) |_meta answer taken_ (<<chk_tf_flow_01,CHK_TF_FLOW_01>>)
|The check looks at every cycle with a meta answer offered. One cycle with `d_ready` at 0 fails it.

|Every request accepted (`REQ_TF_15a`) |_request eventually accepted_ (<<chk_tf_flow_03,CHK_TF_FLOW_03>>)
|The tool looks for a run where a request waits for ever while the ports keep accepting. Finding
one fails the check.

|Every request answered (`REQ_TF_15b`) |_request eventually answered_ (<<chk_tf_flow_04,CHK_TF_FLOW_04>>)
|The tool looks for a run where an accepted request is never answered while the ports keep
answering. Finding one fails the check.

|No request answered twice (`REQ_TF_15c`) |_no extra answer_ (<<chk_tf_flow_02,CHK_TF_FLOW_02>>)
|The first answer uses up the request's credit, so a second answer fails the check.
|===

*Cases:* _two outstanding_, two requests outstanding; _meta FIFO full_, a meta answer arriving
while the FIFO is full; _host answer held_, a host answer held for many cycles while meta answers
arrive; _deadlock precondition_, an engine request at the RMW filter while the core's meta answer
waits for its host answer.

*Never:* a meta answer refused; an answer with no request; a request never accepted, or never
answered.

*Run:* _meta answer taken_ and _no extra answer_ in V1. The two liveness checks in the liveness
run, the checker 1 task where every request is answered (`task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered`).

*Blocked by:* questions an open question and an open question, for the liveness checks.

=== WTRC

What the WTRC does, its sequence and its terms: checker 1 requirements, WTRC.

.Testpoints of the WTRC
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_wtrc_store,wtrc_store>> |A capability store to the NVM goes out as a `Get`, makes no lookup, and each word gets one untagged `AccessAck`.
|<<tp_wtrc_compare,wtrc_compare>> |The tag is set only when both words match the NVM, after W1's NVM answer and ahead of any later lookup; a mismatch gives an error and no alert.
|<<tp_wtrc_faults,wtrc_faults>> |A faulty word (bad integrity, partial, out of sequence) is answered with an error, writes no tag and raises the fatal alert.
|===

[[tp_wtrc_store]]
==== wtrc_store: a capability store to the NVM reads, never writes

*Rule:* each word of a capability store to the NVM reaches the host port as a `Get` of its word,
with a valid command integrity. W0 makes no meta request, and W1 none but its tag write. Each word
is answered once, as an `AccessAck`, untagged, with its `a_source` as `d_source` and a valid
response integrity.

*Observed at:* the core port, the host port, the meta port.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_wtrc_store_01]]`CHK_WTRC_STORE_01` |sent as a full-word Get |forward |A capability store word presented and not yet forwarded is
presented on the host port as a full-word `Get` of the word it targets.
|[[chk_wtrc_store_02]]`CHK_WTRC_STORE_02` |Get has valid command integrity |forward |That `Get` has a valid command integrity.
|[[chk_wtrc_store_03]]`CHK_WTRC_STORE_03` |no lookup for a capability store |backward |No meta request is presented for a capability store
word, except W1's tag write.
|[[chk_wtrc_store_04]]`CHK_WTRC_STORE_04` |untagged AccessAck answer |forward |Each word's answer is an `AccessAck`, untagged, with
`d_source` equal to its `a_source` and a valid response integrity.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Sent as a `Get`, never a write (`REQ_WTRC_01`) |_sent as a full-word Get_ (<<chk_wtrc_store_01,CHK_WTRC_STORE_01>>)
|The check requires a `Get` on the host port for every word. A write reaching the NVM fails it.

|The `Get` has a valid integrity (`REQ_WTRC_02`) |_Get has valid command integrity_ (<<chk_wtrc_store_02,CHK_WTRC_STORE_02>>)
|The check recomputes the `Get`{empty}'s command integrity. The store's own integrity, left on the
`Get`, fails it.

|W0 makes no meta request (`REQ_WTRC_03a`) |_no lookup for a capability store_ (<<chk_wtrc_store_03,CHK_WTRC_STORE_03>>)
|Any meta request presented for W0 fails the check.

|W1 makes none but its tag write (`REQ_WTRC_03b`) |_no lookup for a capability store_ (<<chk_wtrc_store_03,CHK_WTRC_STORE_03>>)
|For W1 only the tag write is allowed; any other meta request fails the check.

|Each word answered once (`REQ_WTRC_05a`) |`tf_flow` _no extra answer_ (<<chk_tf_flow_02,CHK_TF_FLOW_02>>) and _request eventually answered_ (<<chk_tf_flow_04,CHK_TF_FLOW_04>>)
|The tag filter's own checks count the answers of every request, capability stores included: at
most one, and one in the end.

|Answered with an `AccessAck` (`REQ_WTRC_05b`) |_untagged AccessAck answer_ (<<chk_wtrc_store_04,CHK_WTRC_STORE_04>>)
|The check compares the answer's opcode with `AccessAck`. Any other opcode fails it.

|Answered untagged (`REQ_WTRC_05c`) |_untagged AccessAck answer_ (<<chk_wtrc_store_04,CHK_WTRC_STORE_04>>)
|The check requires tag 0 on the answer. A tagged answer fails it.

|Answered with its own source ID (`REQ_WTRC_05d`) |_untagged AccessAck answer_ (<<chk_wtrc_store_04,CHK_WTRC_STORE_04>>)
|The check compares `d_source` with the word's `a_source`. Another ID fails it.

|Answered with a valid integrity (`REQ_WTRC_05e`) |_untagged AccessAck answer_ (<<chk_wtrc_store_04,CHK_WTRC_STORE_04>>)
|The check recomputes the answer's response integrity. A broken one fails it.

|Other accesses unchanged (`REQ_WTRC_13a`) |`tf_forward` _forwarded unchanged_ (<<chk_tf_forward_01,CHK_TF_FORWARD_01>>)
|The tag filter checks run with the WTRC in place, so a field the WTRC changed on any other access
fails them.

|Other accesses on time (`REQ_WTRC_13b`) |`tf_forward` _forwarded unchanged_ (<<chk_tf_forward_01,CHK_TF_FORWARD_01>>) and _answer on last part_ (<<chk_tf_forward_05,CHK_TF_FORWARD_05>>)
|The same checks require the host request and the answer in the same cycle, with the WTRC in place.
A cycle added by the WTRC fails them.
|===

.Cases: look-alike writes to the NVM and the SRAM
[cols="2,3,2,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Write |On the host port |Meta request |Covered by

|capability store W0 to NVM |`csc` W0 to `0x3000_0400`, tag 1, CHERIoT mode |`Get` |none |this
testpoint
|capability store W1 to NVM |`csc` W1 to `0x3000_0404`, tag 1, CHERIoT mode |`Get` |the tag write,
if matched |<<tp_wtrc_compare>>
|word store to NVM |`sw` to `0x3000_0400`, tag 0 |`PutFullData`, unchanged |lookup, tag 0
|<<tp_tf_lookup>>
|capability store to SRAM |`csc` to `0x1000_1238`, tag 1 |`PutFullData`, unchanged |lookup, tag 1
|<<tp_tf_lookup>>
|NVM store in ePMP mode |`csc` to `0x3000_0400`, tag 1, ePMP mode |`PutFullData`, unchanged |none
|<<tp_tf_lookup>>
|===

*Edge cases:* _first NVM capability_, `0x3000_0000`, and _last NVM capability_, `0x301F_FFF8`.

*Never:* a write on the host port for a capability store; a lookup for W0; a tagged answer; a
broken response integrity on the WTRC's own answer.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, the integrity code.

'''

[[tp_wtrc_compare]]
==== wtrc_compare: which stores set the tag

*Rule:* W0 is answered with `d_error` exactly when it did not match. When W0 and W1 both matched,
W1 issues one tag write of tag 1 to the capability's tag bit, after W1's NVM answer and before any
later lookup, and W1 carries the tag write's error. Otherwise W1 is answered with `d_error` and no
tag write goes out. A mismatch or a failed NVM read raises no alert.

*Precedence:* a faulty word is decided by <<tp_wtrc_faults>>. This testpoint decides the words that
are not faulty.

*Observed at:* the core port, the host port (the NVM's answers), the meta port, the WTRC's fault
input to the alert.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_wtrc_compare_01]]`CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_01` |W0 error on mismatch |forward, backward |W0's answer has `d_error` exactly when W0 did not match.
|[[chk_wtrc_compare_02]]`CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_02` |only the owed tag write |forward |While a tag write is owed, any meta request presented is that tag
write: a write of tag 1 to the capability's tag word and bit.
|[[chk_wtrc_compare_03]]`CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_03` |W1 answered after tag write |forward |W1 is answered only after the tag write's answer, with that
answer's `d_error`.
|[[chk_wtrc_compare_04]]`CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_04` |W1 error on mismatch |forward |When W0 or W1 did not match, W1's answer has `d_error` and no tag
write is owed.
|[[chk_wtrc_compare_05]]`CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_05` |no alert without a cause |backward |The WTRC's fault input rises only after a faulty word has
occurred since reset.
|[[chk_wtrc_compare_06]]`CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_06` |answer after NVM answer |backward |Each word is answered only once its NVM answer has arrived, now
or before.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|W0 error when not matched (`REQ_WTRC_04a`) |_W0 error on mismatch_ (<<chk_wtrc_compare_01,CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_01>>), _answer after NVM answer_ (<<chk_wtrc_compare_06,CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_06>>)
|The first check requires `d_error` on every W0 that did not match. The second makes sure W0 waits
for the NVM answer that decides whether it matched.

|No W0 error when matched (`REQ_WTRC_04b`) |_W0 error on mismatch_ (<<chk_wtrc_compare_01,CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_01>>)
|The check runs in both directions: a matched W0 answered with `d_error` fails it.

|The tag write sets tag 1 at the right bit (`REQ_WTRC_06a`) |_only the owed tag write_ (<<chk_wtrc_compare_02,CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_02>>), _W1 answered after tag write_ (<<chk_wtrc_compare_03,CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_03>>)
|The first check fixes what the tag write carries: tag 1, the right word and bit. The second makes
it happen: W1 cannot be answered until the tag write is answered.

|Tag write only after W1's NVM answer (`REQ_WTRC_06b`) |_only the owed tag write_ (<<chk_wtrc_compare_02,CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_02>>) with `tf_lookup` _no unneeded lookup_ (<<chk_tf_lookup_02,CHK_TF_LOOKUP_02>>)
|A tag write is owed only from W1's NVM answer on. One issued earlier is not owed, so it is a meta
request with no credit, and the lookup check fails.

|Tag write ahead of any later lookup (`REQ_WTRC_06c`) |_only the owed tag write_ (<<chk_wtrc_compare_02,CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_02>>)
|While the tag write is owed, the only meta request allowed is the tag write. A lookup presented
first fails the check.

|W1 error when the tag write fails (`REQ_WTRC_07a`) |_W1 answered after tag write_ (<<chk_wtrc_compare_03,CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_03>>)
|The check requires W1's `d_error` to equal the tag write's. A lost error fails it.

|No W1 error when the tag write succeeds (`REQ_WTRC_07b`) |_W1 answered after tag write_ (<<chk_wtrc_compare_03,CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_03>>)
|The same equality: an error invented on W1 fails it.

|W1 error when not matched (`REQ_WTRC_08a`) |_W1 error on mismatch_ (<<chk_wtrc_compare_04,CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_04>>)
|When W0 or W1 did not match, the check requires `d_error` on W1.

|No tag write when not matched (`REQ_WTRC_08b`) |_W1 error on mismatch_ (<<chk_wtrc_compare_04,CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_04>>) with `tf_lookup` _no unneeded lookup_ (<<chk_tf_lookup_02,CHK_TF_LOOKUP_02>>)
|After a mismatch no tag write is owed, so a tag write is a meta request with no credit, and the
lookup check fails.

|No alert for a mismatch (`REQ_WTRC_09`) |_no alert without a cause_ (<<chk_wtrc_compare_05,CHK_WTRC_COMPARE_05>>)
|The fault input may rise only after a faulty word. A mismatch or a failed NVM read is not one, so
an alert for it fails the check. "Since reset" is enough because the alert stays raised until
reset.
|===

.Truth table: one cover per row
[cols="3,2,2,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |W0, W1 matched |Tag write error |Tag write |`d_error` on W0, W1

|both match, tag write ok |1, 1 |0 |yes, tag 1 |0, 0
|both match, tag write error |1, 1 |1 |yes, tag 1 |0, 1
|W1 mismatch |1, 0 |- |none |0, 1
|W0 mismatch |0, 1 |- |none |1, 1
|both mismatch |0, 0 |- |none |1, 1
|===

.Cases: one cause of a mismatch at a time, each covered for W0 and for W1
[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Cause

|NVM read error |the NVM read answers with `d_error`
|data differ in bit 0 |the data differ from the NVM's in bit 0
|data differ in bit 31 |the data differ from the NVM's in bit 31
|only integrity differs |the data equal the NVM's, the data integrity differs
|===

*Edge cases:* _last NVM tag write_, the tag write of the last NVM capability, `0x301F_FFF8`: word
`0x1100_8BFC`, bit 31; _W0 in W1's answer cycle_, a W0 presented in the cycle the previous
capability's W1 is answered.

*Never:* a tag write after a mismatch; a tag write before W1's NVM answer, or behind a later
lookup; a word answered before its NVM answer; an alert for a mismatch or a failed NVM read.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, the bit of the tag write.

'''

[[tp_wtrc_faults]]
==== wtrc_faults: what the core cannot produce

*Rule:* a faulty word is answered with `d_error`, writes no tag and raises `fatal_fault`. Any other
request out of the sequence of a capability store raises `fatal_fault`.

*Observed at:* the core port, the meta port, the alert sender's request input.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_wtrc_faults_01]]`CHK_WTRC_FAULTS_01` |faulty word answered with error |forward |A faulty word is answered with `d_error`, and no tag
write is owed for its capability.
|[[chk_wtrc_faults_02]]`CHK_WTRC_FAULTS_02` |faulty word raises alert |liveness |A faulty word raises the alert request in the end.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Faulty word answered with an error (`REQ_WTRC_10a`) |_faulty word answered with error_ (<<chk_wtrc_faults_01,CHK_WTRC_FAULTS_01>>)
|The check requires `d_error` on every faulty word. A faulty word answered cleanly fails it.

|Faulty word writes no tag (`REQ_WTRC_10b`) |_faulty word answered with error_ (<<chk_wtrc_faults_01,CHK_WTRC_FAULTS_01>>) with `tf_lookup` _no unneeded lookup_ (<<chk_tf_lookup_02,CHK_TF_LOOKUP_02>>)
|No tag write is owed after a faulty word, so a tag write is a meta request with no credit, and the
lookup check fails.

|Faulty word raises the alert (`REQ_WTRC_11`) |_faulty word raises alert_ (<<chk_wtrc_faults_02,CHK_WTRC_FAULTS_02>>)
|The spec gives no time from the fault to the alert, so the check has no bound. It needs no
fairness: nothing outside the design holds the alert back.

|Other request out of sequence raises the alert (`REQ_WTRC_12`) |no check
|Only a core that breaks its access order sends such a request, and that core is out of scope
(xref:{tp}#not_covered[not covered]).
|===

A word out of sequence or partial also needs a core that breaks its access order or sends a tagged
partial write, which is out of scope too. The two checks are reached through the integrity faults
below.

.Cases: the integrity faults
[cols="2,2,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |State |Request |Result

|bad data integrity |W0 taken |W1 with a bad data integrity |`d_error`, no tag, alert
|bad command integrity |no capability open |W0 with a bad command integrity |`d_error`, alert
|bad NVM response integrity |W0 taken |W0's NVM answer with a bad response integrity |`d_error`,
alert
|===

*Edge cases:* _W0 in W1's answer cycle_, a W0 presented in the cycle W1 is answered, is in
sequence: no alert.

*Never:* an alert for a request in sequence and free of integrity faults; a tag write for a faulty
word.

*Run:* V1: integrity is free on every port.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, the integrity code; and a finding: the design
answers a store with a broken command or NVM response integrity without `d_error` and lets W1 write
the tag. The three integrity cases fail until the designers decide
(finding).

=== 2:1 tag arbiter

How the 2:1 tag arbiter works: input 0 is the core's tag filter, input 1 the engine's
(xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc#arb[design architecture doc,
2:1 tag arbiter]). A request leaves the arbiter with `a_source` shifted left by one and the input
number in bit 0, kept to 8 bits; its answer comes back with that bit shifted off.

.Testpoints of the 2:1 tag arbiter
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_arb_forward,arb_forward>> |Each request leaves the arbiter once, unchanged, with its own tag and bit select and its input number added to the source ID.
|<<tp_arb_return,arb_return>> |Each answer goes back only to the input that asked, with its source ID restored and every other field unchanged.
|<<tp_arb_flow,arb_flow>> |Requests and answers pass in the same cycle, and neither input waits for ever.
|===

[[tp_arb_forward]]
==== arb_forward: each request forwarded once, with its own sideband

*Rule:* a request accepted on an input leaves the arbiter once, in the same cycle, with every field
but `a_source` unchanged, its own tag and bit select, and its input number added to `a_source`. A
core request reaches the RMW filter exactly as the arbiter forwards it.

*Observed at:* the arbiter's three ports; the RMW filter's upstream port for the core request.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_arb_forward_01]]`CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01` |keeps its own sideband |forward |A request accepted on input `i` leaves the arbiter in the same
cycle with every field but `a_source` unchanged, its own tag and bit select, and `a_source`
shifted left with `i` in bit 0.
|[[chk_arb_forward_02]]`CHK_ARB_FORWARD_02` |from the named input |backward |A request leaving the arbiter is the request of the input named
by its bit 0, accepted in that cycle.
|[[chk_arb_forward_03]]`CHK_ARB_FORWARD_03` |core request unchanged |forward |A request from input 0 reaches the RMW filter exactly as it
leaves the arbiter: every field, the tag and the bit select.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Every accepted request forwarded (`REQ_ARB_01a`) |_keeps its own sideband_ (<<chk_arb_forward_01,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check requires the forwarded request in the cycle the input request is accepted. A dropped
request fails it.

|No request forwarded twice (`REQ_ARB_01b`) |_from the named input_ (<<chk_arb_forward_02,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_02>>)
|A forwarded request must match an input request accepted in that cycle. A second copy in a later
cycle has none and fails.

|No request invented (`REQ_ARB_02`) |_from the named input_ (<<chk_arb_forward_02,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_02>>)
|A forwarded request with no input request behind it fails the check.

|Address unchanged (`REQ_ARB_03a`) |_keeps its own sideband_ (<<chk_arb_forward_01,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded address with the input request's. Any change fails it.

|Opcode unchanged (`REQ_ARB_03b`) |_keeps its own sideband_ (<<chk_arb_forward_01,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded opcode with the input request's. A changed opcode fails it.

|Size unchanged (`REQ_ARB_03c`) |_keeps its own sideband_ (<<chk_arb_forward_01,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded size with the input request's. A changed size fails it.

|Byte mask unchanged (`REQ_ARB_03d`) |_keeps its own sideband_ (<<chk_arb_forward_01,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded mask with the input request's. A changed mask fails it.

|Data unchanged (`REQ_ARB_03e`) |_keeps its own sideband_ (<<chk_arb_forward_01,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded data with the input request's. A changed bit fails it.

|User bits unchanged (`REQ_ARB_03f`) |_keeps its own sideband_ (<<chk_arb_forward_01,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded `a_user` with the input request's. A changed bit fails it.

|Its own tag (`REQ_ARB_04a`) |_keeps its own sideband_ (<<chk_arb_forward_01,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded tag with that of the input it came from. The other input's tag
fails it; the case _worked example_ sends different tags on both inputs at once.

|Its own bit select (`REQ_ARB_04b`) |_keeps its own sideband_ (<<chk_arb_forward_01,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded bit select with that of its input. The other input's bit select
fails it.

|Core request unchanged up to the RMW filter (`REQ_ARB_11`) |_core request unchanged_ (<<chk_arb_forward_03,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_03>>)
|The check compares the request at the RMW filter with the arbiter's output. Any change by the
stage in between fails it.
|===

*Cases:* _input 0 alone_; _input 1 alone_; _both, input 0 wins_ and _both, input 1 wins_; _input 1
back to back_; _worked example_, a write of tag 1 to bit 7 on input 0 and a read of bit 8 on input
1 in one cycle.

*Edge cases:* _source 0x00_ on each input; _source 0x7F_ on input 1 and _source 0x1F_ on input 0,
the largest source each requester sends; _bit select 0_ and _bit select 31_.

*Never:* a request no input presented; one input's tag or bit select on the other's request; a
core request changed between the arbiter and the RMW filter.

*Run:* V1.

'''

[[tp_arb_return]]
==== arb_return: each answer to the input that asked

*Rule:* an answer goes only to the input named by bit 0 of its `d_source`, with `d_source` shifted
back right and every other field and the tag unchanged.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_arb_return_01]]`CHK_ARB_RETURN_01` |answer to its input |backward |An answer at input `i` is the RMW filter's answer of that cycle,
with bit 0 of its `d_source` equal to `i`.
|[[chk_arb_return_02]]`CHK_ARB_RETURN_02` |taken with its input |forward, backward |The RMW filter's answer is taken in the cycle its input
takes it, and only then.
|[[chk_arb_return_03]]`CHK_ARB_RETURN_03` |source shifted back |forward |That answer carries the RMW filter's `d_source` shifted right by one.
|[[chk_arb_return_04]]`CHK_ARB_RETURN_04` |fields unchanged |forward |Every other field of the answer, and the tag, is unchanged.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Answer reaches the input that asked (`REQ_ARB_05a`) |_taken with its input_ (<<chk_arb_return_02,CHK_ARB_RETURN_02>>)
|The RMW filter's answer may be taken only when its own input takes it. An answer lost on the way
is taken by no input and fails the check.

|Answer reaches no other input (`REQ_ARB_05b`) |_answer to its input_ (<<chk_arb_return_01,CHK_ARB_RETURN_01>>)
|An answer at an input whose number is not bit 0 of `d_source` fails the check, and so does an
answer at both inputs.

|Its own source ID back (`REQ_ARB_06`) |_source shifted back_ (<<chk_arb_return_03,CHK_ARB_RETURN_03>>), with `arb_forward` _keeps its own sideband_ (<<chk_arb_forward_01,CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01>>)
|The way out adds the input bit, the RMW filter returns the ID unchanged, and this check removes the
bit. Together the requester gets back the `a_source` it sent, while its top bit is 0 (question
an open question).

|Answer's opcode unchanged (`REQ_ARB_07a`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_arb_return_04,CHK_ARB_RETURN_04>>)
|The check compares the answer's opcode at the input with the RMW filter's. Any change fails it.

|Answer's size unchanged (`REQ_ARB_07b`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_arb_return_04,CHK_ARB_RETURN_04>>)
|The check compares the answer's size at the input with the RMW filter's. Any change fails it.

|Answer's data unchanged (`REQ_ARB_07c`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_arb_return_04,CHK_ARB_RETURN_04>>)
|The check compares the answer's data at the input with the RMW filter's. Any change fails it.

|Answer's error bit unchanged (`REQ_ARB_07d`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_arb_return_04,CHK_ARB_RETURN_04>>)
|The check compares `d_error` at the input with the RMW filter's. A hidden or invented error fails
it.

|Answer's user bits unchanged (`REQ_ARB_07e`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_arb_return_04,CHK_ARB_RETURN_04>>)
|The check compares `d_user` at the input with the RMW filter's. Any change fails it.

|Answer's tag unchanged (`REQ_ARB_07f`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_arb_return_04,CHK_ARB_RETURN_04>>)
|The check compares the tag at the input with the RMW filter's. A changed tag fails it.
|===

*Cases:* _answer to input 0_ and _answer to input 1_; _alternating inputs_, answers to alternating
inputs in consecutive cycles; _source 0x02 to input 0_, `0x02` goes to input 0 as `0x01`; _source
0x03 to input 1_, `0x03` goes to input 1 as `0x01`.

*Never:* an answer at both inputs, or at the input that did not ask.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, the free top bit of the core's source ID.

'''

[[tp_arb_flow]]
==== arb_flow: no added cycle, no starvation

*Rule:* a request alone reaches the RMW filter in the cycle it is presented, and an answer reaches
its input in the cycle the RMW filter gives it. A request held on either input is accepted in the
end, given the RMW filter keeps accepting.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_arb_flow_01]]`CHK_ARB_FLOW_01` |alone in same cycle |forward |A request presented on one input while the other presents none is
presented to the RMW filter in the same cycle.
|[[chk_arb_flow_02]]`CHK_ARB_FLOW_02` |answer at once |forward |The RMW filter's answer is presented at its input in the same cycle.
|[[chk_arb_flow_03]]`CHK_ARB_FLOW_03` |no starvation |liveness |A request held on either input is accepted in the end, given the RMW
filter keeps accepting.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|No input waits for ever (`REQ_ARB_08`) |_no starvation_ (<<chk_arb_flow_03,CHK_ARB_FLOW_03>>)
|The tool looks for a run where one input waits for ever while the other keeps winning. The case
_starvation case_ keeps input 1 busy in every cycle. Finding such a run fails the check.

|Request alone passes in the same cycle (`REQ_ARB_09`) |_alone in same cycle_ (<<chk_arb_flow_01,CHK_ARB_FLOW_01>>)
|The check requires the request at the RMW filter in the very cycle it is presented. A cycle added
fails it.

|Answer passes in the same cycle (`REQ_ARB_10`) |_answer at once_ (<<chk_arb_flow_02,CHK_ARB_FLOW_02>>)
|The check requires the answer at its input in the cycle the RMW filter gives it. A cycle added
fails it.
|===

*Cases:* _input 0 alone_; _input 1 alone_; _starvation case_, input 1 presenting in every cycle
while input 0 waits.

*Never:* a cycle added on the way out or back; an input starved.

*Run:* the two same-cycle checks in V1; _no starvation_ in the liveness run
(`task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered`).

*Blocked by:* question an open question, the arbitration policy, for _no starvation_.

=== RMW filter

How the RMW filter works: xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc#rmw[design
architecture doc, RMW filter]. In this section, "the bit" of a word is the bit the request's bit
select names, and "the updated word" is the read word with that bit set to the tag and every other
bit kept.

.Testpoints of the RMW filter
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_rmw_read,rmw_read>> |A read fetches its meta word and returns the right bit; back-to-back reads run at one per cycle.
|<<tp_rmw_write_skip,rmw_write_skip>> |A write reads its word first; if the bit already equals the tag it skips the write-back and answers with an `AccessAck`.
|<<tp_rmw_write_back,rmw_write_back>> |A changed bit is written back alone, as a full-word `PutFullData` with fresh integrity, and its answer is passed up.
|<<tp_rmw_single_op,rmw_single_op>> |One operation at a time, every request answered once, and nothing else sent to the meta SRAM.
|<<tp_rmw_errors,rmw_errors>> |A device error aborts the write-back and reaches the requester; no error is invented.
|===

[[tp_rmw_read]]
==== rmw_read: a read returns its bit

*Rule:* a read issues one `Get` of its meta word to the meta SRAM, and its answer's tag is the bit
of the word read. A read presented in the cycle the previous read is answered is accepted then, if
the meta SRAM side is ready. Every `Get` carries a valid command integrity.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_rmw_read_01]]`CHK_RMW_READ_01` |Get of its meta word |forward |A read's request to the meta SRAM is a `Get` of its meta word, with
its `a_source`.
|[[chk_rmw_read_02]]`CHK_RMW_READ_02` |returns its tag bit |forward |A read's answer without `d_error` has as its tag the bit of the
word its `Get` returned.
|[[chk_rmw_read_03]]`CHK_RMW_READ_03` |back-to-back read accepted |forward |A read presented in the cycle the previous read is answered,
with the meta SRAM side ready, is accepted in that cycle.
|[[chk_rmw_read_04]]`CHK_RMW_READ_04` |Get carries valid integrity |forward |Every `Get` presented to the meta SRAM carries a valid
command integrity.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Read forwarded at its meta word (`REQ_RMW_01`) |_Get of its meta word_ (<<chk_rmw_read_01,CHK_RMW_READ_01>>)
|The check compares the `Get`{empty}'s address with the read's meta word. Another word fails it.

|Read returns its bit (`REQ_RMW_02`) |_returns its tag bit_ (<<chk_rmw_read_02,CHK_RMW_READ_02>>)
|The check picks the bit out of the word read and compares it with the answer's tag. Another bit
fails it; the word cases make every neighbour bit differ.

|Back-to-back reads at one per cycle (`REQ_RMW_11`) |_back-to-back read accepted_ (<<chk_rmw_read_03,CHK_RMW_READ_03>>)
|The check requires the next read to be accepted in the cycle the previous one is answered. A
cycle lost fails it.

|Every `Get` has a valid integrity (`REQ_RMW_18`) |_Get carries valid integrity_ (<<chk_rmw_read_04,CHK_RMW_READ_04>>)
|The check recomputes the command integrity of every `Get`, for reads and writes. Nothing else
checks it: the TL-UL bus checker leaves integrity free.
|===

*Cases:* the word read, _word all zeros_ `0x0000_0000`, _word all ones_ `0xFFFF_FFFF`, _word AAAA_
`0xAAAA_AAAA`, _word 5555_ `0x5555_5555` and _word with one bit_, a single bit at the bit select;
the bit select, _bit select 0_, _bit select 7_, _bit select 31_; _reads back to back_, reads in
consecutive cycles.

*Never:* a read turned into a write; the tag of another bit.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for the integrity check.

'''

[[tp_rmw_write_skip]]
==== rmw_write_skip: an equal bit is not written

*Rule:* a write first issues a full-word `Get` of its meta word. If the bit already equals the tag,
the write issues no write-back and is answered with an `AccessAck`, once the `Get`{empty}'s answer
has arrived.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_rmw_write_skip_01]]`CHK_RMW_WRITE_SKIP_01` |full-word Get first |forward |A write's first request to the meta SRAM is a full-word `Get` of its
meta word.
|[[chk_rmw_write_skip_02]]`CHK_RMW_WRITE_SKIP_02` |no write-back |backward |No write-back is presented for a write whose `Get` answer has its bit
equal to the tag.
|[[chk_rmw_write_skip_03]]`CHK_RMW_WRITE_SKIP_03` |answered with AccessAck |forward |Such a write is answered with an `AccessAck`.
|[[chk_rmw_write_skip_04]]`CHK_RMW_WRITE_SKIP_04` |answer after Get answer |backward |A write is answered only once its `Get`{empty}'s answer has
arrived, now or before.
|===

_No write-back_ and _answered with AccessAck_ claim nothing after a faulty `Get` answer.

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Write reads its word first (`REQ_RMW_03`) |_full-word Get first_ (<<chk_rmw_write_skip_01,CHK_RMW_WRITE_SKIP_01>>), _answer after Get answer_ (<<chk_rmw_write_skip_04,CHK_RMW_WRITE_SKIP_04>>)
|The first check requires a full-word `Get` as the write's first request. The second makes sure
the write is not answered before that `Get` comes back.

|Equal bit: no write-back (`REQ_RMW_04`) |_no write-back_ (<<chk_rmw_write_skip_02,CHK_RMW_WRITE_SKIP_02>>)
|A write-back presented when the bit already equals the tag fails the check.

|Equal bit: answered with an `AccessAck` (`REQ_RMW_05`) |_answered with AccessAck_ (<<chk_rmw_write_skip_03,CHK_RMW_WRITE_SKIP_03>>), _answer after Get answer_ (<<chk_rmw_write_skip_04,CHK_RMW_WRITE_SKIP_04>>)
|The first check compares the answer's opcode with `AccessAck`. The second makes sure it comes
only once the `Get` answer has arrived.
|===

.Truth table: stored bit and tag to write
[cols="2,1,1,2,3",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Stored bit |Tag |Write-back |Testpoint

|bit and tag 0 |0 |0 |no |this one
|bit and tag 1 |1 |1 |no |this one
|tag 1 over stored 0 |0 |1 |yes |<<tp_rmw_write_back>>
|tag 0 over stored 1 |1 |0 |yes |<<tp_rmw_write_back>>
|===

*Cases:* _core write's Get_, a write from the core's tag filter; _engine write's Get_, a write from
the engine's tag filter.

*Never:* a write-back when the bit is equal; a write with no `Get` first; a write answered before
its `Get`{empty}'s answer.

*Run:* V1.

'''

[[tp_rmw_write_back]]
==== rmw_write_back: a changed bit is written back alone

*Rule:* if the bit differs from the tag, the filter writes back the updated word with one full-word
`PutFullData` to the same meta word, with freshly computed command and data integrity. The
write-back's answer is forwarded as the write's answer. Every request the write issues carries its
`a_source`.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_rmw_write_back_01]]`CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_01` |carries the updated word |forward |The write-back of a write whose bit differs carries the updated
word.
|[[chk_rmw_write_back_02]]`CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_02` |full-word Put to same word |forward |It is a full-word `PutFullData` to the same meta word, with a
valid command integrity and a valid data integrity.
|[[chk_rmw_write_back_03]]`CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_03` |write-back answer passed up |forward |Such a write is answered only with its write-back's answer,
in the same cycle, carrying its `d_opcode` and `d_error`.
|[[chk_rmw_write_back_04]]`CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_04` |keeps the write's source |forward |Every request a write issues to the meta SRAM carries the
write's `a_source`.
|===

These checks claim nothing after a faulty `Get` answer.

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|The bit set to the tag (`REQ_RMW_06a`) |_carries the updated word_ (<<chk_rmw_write_back_01,CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_01>>)
|The check computes the updated word from the word read and compares it with the write-back. A
bit not set to the tag fails it.

|Every other bit kept (`REQ_RMW_06b`) |_carries the updated word_ (<<chk_rmw_write_back_01,CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_01>>)
|The same comparison covers all 32 bits, so any other bit changed fails it. The word cases make
every neighbour bit 0 or 1.

|A full-word `PutFullData` to the same word (`REQ_RMW_07a`) |_full-word Put to same word_ (<<chk_rmw_write_back_02,CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_02>>)
|The check compares the opcode, the size, the mask and the address with a full-word write to the
word read. Any difference fails it.

|Fresh command integrity (`REQ_RMW_07b`) |_full-word Put to same word_ (<<chk_rmw_write_back_02,CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_02>>)
|The check recomputes the write-back's command integrity. The `Get`{empty}'s integrity left in
place fails it.

|Fresh data integrity (`REQ_RMW_07c`) |_full-word Put to same word_ (<<chk_rmw_write_back_02,CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_02>>)
|The check recomputes the data integrity over the updated word. The integrity of the word read
fails it, because one bit changed.

|Write-back's answer passed up (`REQ_RMW_08`) |_write-back answer passed up_ (<<chk_rmw_write_back_03,CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_03>>)
|The check requires the write's answer in the cycle of the write-back's answer, with its opcode
and error. An answer taken from the `Get` fails it.

|The write's source ID on every request (`REQ_RMW_09`) |_keeps the write's source_ (<<chk_rmw_write_back_04,CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_04>>)
|The check compares the `a_source` of the `Get` and of the write-back with the write's. Another ID
fails it.
|===

.Cases
[cols="2,2,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Word read |Write |Word written back

|clear bit 7 |`0x0000_0080` |tag 0 to bit 7 |`0x0000_0000`
|set bit 8 |`0x0000_0080` |tag 1 to bit 8 |`0x0000_0180`
|clear bit 31 |`0xFFFF_FFFF` |tag 0 to bit 31 |`0x7FFF_FFFF`
|set bit 0 |`0x0000_0000` |tag 1 to bit 0 |`0x0000_0001`
|set bit in word AAAA |`0xAAAA_AAAA` |tag 1 to bit 0 |`0xAAAA_AAAB`
|===

*Never:* any other bit changed; a write-back to another word; a stale integrity; a second
write-back.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for the integrity checks; question
an open question, for a write-back after a faulty `Get` answer.

'''

[[tp_rmw_single_op]]
==== rmw_single_op: one operation at a time

*Rule:* a new request is accepted only when no operation is unanswered, or in the cycle the only
unanswered operation, a read, is answered. Every accepted request is answered once, given the meta
SRAM answers. The meta SRAM side carries one `Get` per accepted request, plus one write-back for a
write whose bit changes, and nothing else.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_rmw_single_op_01]]`CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_01` |one operation at a time |backward |A request is accepted only when no operation is unanswered, or
in the cycle the only unanswered operation, a read, is answered.
|[[chk_rmw_single_op_02]]`CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_02` |nothing else downstream |backward |Every request to the meta SRAM is the `Get` of the current or
the presented request, or the write-back of the current write whose bit differs, each once.
|[[chk_rmw_single_op_03]]`CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_03` |one answer per operation |backward |An answer is presented upstream only while an operation is
unanswered.
|[[chk_rmw_single_op_04]]`CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_04` |every operation answered |liveness |Every accepted request is answered in the end, given the meta
SRAM answers.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|One operation at a time (`REQ_RMW_10`) |_one operation at a time_ (<<chk_rmw_single_op_01,CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_01>>)
|A request accepted while an earlier operation is still unanswered, other than a read answered in
that cycle, fails the check.

|Every request answered (`REQ_RMW_15a`) |_every operation answered_ (<<chk_rmw_single_op_04,CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_04>>)
|The tool looks for a run where an operation is never answered while the meta SRAM answers. Finding
one fails the check.

|No request answered twice (`REQ_RMW_15b`) |_one answer per operation_ (<<chk_rmw_single_op_03,CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_03>>)
|After its answer an operation is closed, so a second answer finds no open operation and fails.

|At most one `Get` per request (`REQ_RMW_16a`) |_nothing else downstream_ (<<chk_rmw_single_op_02,CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_02>>)
|Each request allows its `Get` once. A second `Get`, or one with no request, fails the check.

|A write-back only for a changed bit (`REQ_RMW_16b`) |_nothing else downstream_ (<<chk_rmw_single_op_02,CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_02>>)
|A write-back is allowed once, and only for the current write whose bit differs. A write-back for a
read, for an equal bit, or a second one fails the check.
|===

After a faulty `Get` answer the write-back slot of _nothing else downstream_ stays open until the
write is answered: what the filter sends there is not claimed.

*Cases:* _write then read_, a read waiting for a write's write-back answer; _reads back to back_;
_write then write_; _filters interleaved_, requests from both tag filters interleaved.

*Never:* two operations in flight; a write-back for a read; a request to the meta SRAM with no
request upstream.

*Run:* the three backward checks in V1; _every operation answered_ in the liveness run
(`task_TagPath_EveryReqAnswered`).

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for _every operation answered_.

'''

[[tp_rmw_errors]]
==== rmw_errors: device errors

*Rule:* a device error on the `Get` of a write aborts it: no write-back. A device error on any meta
SRAM answer reaches the requester as `d_error`, and only such an answer does.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_rmw_errors_01]]`CHK_RMW_ERRORS_01` |Get error stops the write |backward |No write-back is presented for a write whose `Get` answer has
`d_error`.
|[[chk_rmw_errors_02]]`CHK_RMW_ERRORS_02` |error passed up |forward |An operation whose answer from the meta SRAM has `d_error` is answered
upstream with `d_error`.
|[[chk_rmw_errors_03]]`CHK_RMW_ERRORS_03` |no error without a cause |backward |An answer upstream has `d_error` only when its operation's
`Get` answer or write-back answer has `d_error`.
|===

_Error passed up_ and _no error without a cause_ claim nothing after a faulty `Get` answer.

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|`Get` error aborts the write (`REQ_RMW_13`) |_Get error stops the write_ (<<chk_rmw_errors_01,CHK_RMW_ERRORS_01>>)
|A write-back presented after a `Get` answer with `d_error` fails the check, whether or not the bit
differs.

|Device error reaches the requester (`REQ_RMW_14`) |_error passed up_ (<<chk_rmw_errors_02,CHK_RMW_ERRORS_02>>)
|The check requires `d_error` upstream for every operation with an error from the meta SRAM. A lost
error fails it.

|No error without a cause (`REQ_RMW_17`) |_no error without a cause_ (<<chk_rmw_errors_03,CHK_RMW_ERRORS_03>>)
|An answer with `d_error` whose `Get` and write-back answers had none fails the check.
|===

*Cases:* _read answer error_; _Get error, bit equal_; _Get error, bit differs_; _write-back
error_.

*Never:* a write-back after an errored `Get`; an error not passed up; an error upstream with no
error from the meta SRAM.

*Run:* V1.

=== Tag path end to end

These rows hold for the tag path as a whole and are checked at the alert sender.

.Testpoints of the tag path
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_tag_alerts,tag_alerts>> |A device error or an integrity fault on the tag path raises the fatal alert, which stays raised until reset.
|===

[[tp_tag_alerts]]
==== tag_alerts: the tag path's faults raise the alert

*Rule:* a device error or an integrity fault on a meta SRAM answer to the tag path requests
`fatal_fault`. Once raised, the alert stays raised until reset.

*Observed at:* the alert sender's request input.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tag_alerts_01]]`CHK_TAG_ALERTS_01` |device error raises alert |liveness |A meta SRAM answer the RMW filter takes with `d_error`
raises the alert request in the end.
|[[chk_tag_alerts_02]]`CHK_TAG_ALERTS_02` |integrity fault raises alert |liveness |A meta SRAM answer the RMW filter takes with a broken
response or data integrity raises the alert request in the end.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Device error raises the alert (`REQ_TAG_07`) |_device error raises alert_ (<<chk_tag_alerts_01,CHK_TAG_ALERTS_01>>)
|The tool looks for a run where such an answer never raises the alert request. The spec gives no
time, so the check has no bound; nothing outside the design holds it back.

|Integrity fault raises the alert (`REQ_TAG_08`) |_integrity fault raises alert_ (<<chk_tag_alerts_02,CHK_TAG_ALERTS_02>>)
|The same, for an answer with a broken integrity, with or without `d_error`.

|Alert stays raised (`REQ_TAG_10`) |no check in checker 1
|The alert sender, built as a fatal alert, keeps signalling once requested until reset. That is
the sender's own design, verified by its own testbench (premise P2 of the TB architecture).
|===

*Cases:* _read answer error_; _write Get error_; _write-back error_; _bad response integrity_;
_bad data integrity_; _both integrities bad_; _write Get integrity bad_, a write's `Get` answered
with a broken integrity and no `d_error`.

*Never:* a tag path fault with no alert request.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for _integrity fault raises alert_.

=== Open items

The questions that block a check, each explained in the requirements doc:

(<<tp_tf_meta_request>>, <<tp_wtrc_compare>>).
|an open question |The tag filter's _no extra host request_ and _request eventually answered_
(<<tp_tf_forward>>, <<tp_tf_flow>>).

(<<tp_rmw_write_back>>).
