[[checker2]]
== Checker 2: meta access


=== Terms

The request and address terms shared with the other checkers (CHERIoT mode `Ena`, `Get`, `Wr`, a
legal request `Legal`, a port's region `InRegion`, a full word `FullWord`, a valid integrity
`IntgOk` and the like) are in the xref:{tp}#terms[main testplan, Terms]. The terms only checker 2
uses:

[cols="2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Term |Meaning

|Input, port `i` |The number of the 4:1 arbiter input a requester port is wired to: 0
`corerevbm_tl` (the core's TRVK filter), 1 the tag port (the RMW filter, for both tag filters), 2
`revbm_tl_d` (software, through `xbar_main`), 3 the revocation engine's bitmap port. Input 1 owns
the tag regions `0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF`; the other three own the revocation bitmap
`0x1100_0000`-`0x1100_0BFF`. Port `i` in a cover formula is the port on input `i`. Which port sits
on which input is wiring: each check uses its own port's number, so no expected value depends on it.
|Checked stream |An access checker's output: a host port of the 4:1 arbiter.
|Grant |The 4:1 arbiter forwards a request from one of its host ports to `meta_sram_tl`.
|Forwarded source ID |The `a_source` a request from input `i` carries on `meta_sram_tl`: its own
`a_source` shifted left by two, with the input number in the two lowest bits.
|Answer's input, returned source ID |An answer on `meta_sram_tl` belongs to the input named in the
two lowest bits of its `d_source`, and reaches it with `d_source` shifted right by two.
|Refused request, error answer |A request on a requester port that is not legal is refused. The
answer its access checker gives it, from its own error responder, is its error answer.
|===

=== Access checkers and 4:1 arbiter

How the access checkers and the 4:1 arbiter work:
xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc#tag_sharing[design architecture doc, Sharing
the meta SRAM].

.Testpoints of the access checkers and the 4:1 arbiter
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_meta_forward,meta_forward>> |A legal request reaches `meta_sram_tl` once, every field unchanged but its source ID, in the cycle it is presented when no other port presents one; nothing else reaches it.
|<<tp_meta_refuse,meta_refuse>> |A refused request never reaches `meta_sram_tl` and gets one error answer, with `d_error` and a valid integrity.
|<<tp_meta_return,meta_return>> |Each meta SRAM answer reaches only the port that asked, in the cycle it arrives, its source ID shifted back and every other field unchanged.
|<<tp_meta_flow,meta_flow>> |The arbiter grants in round robin; every held request is accepted and every accepted request answered exactly once.
|===

[[tp_meta_forward]]
==== meta_forward: a legal request reaches the meta SRAM once, unchanged

*Rule:* a legal request on a requester port is forwarded to `meta_sram_tl` exactly once. Every
A-channel field stays unchanged except `a_source`, which becomes the forwarded source ID. A legal
request presented while no other port presents one reaches `meta_sram_tl` in the cycle it is
presented. `meta_sram_tl` carries nothing else.

*Observed at:* the four requester ports and `meta_sram_tl`.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_meta_forward_01]]`CHK_META_FORWARD_01` |legal request forwarded |forward |A legal request presented on a requester port appears on
`meta_sram_tl` with the same `a_opcode`, `a_param`, `a_address`, `a_size`, `a_mask`, `a_data` and
`a_user` (its integrity included) and the forwarded source ID; in the cycle it is presented when no
other port presents one.
|[[chk_meta_forward_02]]`CHK_META_FORWARD_02` |no extra meta SRAM request |backward |Every request on `meta_sram_tl` belongs to one legal request presented
on a requester port and not yet forwarded: none invented, none forwarded twice.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Legal request forwarded (`REQ_META_01a`) |_legal request forwarded_ (<<chk_meta_forward_01,CHK_META_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check requires every legal request presented to appear on `meta_sram_tl`. A legal request
dropped, or refused with an error answer, never appears and fails it.

|Forwarded at most once (`REQ_META_01b`) |_no extra meta SRAM request_ (<<chk_meta_forward_02,CHK_META_FORWARD_02>>)
|A request on `meta_sram_tl` must match a legal request not yet forwarded. A second copy finds its
request already forwarded and fails the check.

|Opcode unchanged (`REQ_META_02a`) |_legal request forwarded_ (<<chk_meta_forward_01,CHK_META_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded `a_opcode` with the requester's. A `Get` turned into a
`PutFullData`, or the reverse, fails it.

|Param unchanged (`REQ_META_02b`) |_legal request forwarded_ (<<chk_meta_forward_01,CHK_META_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded `a_param` with the requester's. Any changed bit fails it.

|Address unchanged (`REQ_META_02c`) |_legal request forwarded_ (<<chk_meta_forward_01,CHK_META_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded `a_address` with the requester's. Any changed bit fails it.

|Data unchanged (`REQ_META_02d`) |_legal request forwarded_ (<<chk_meta_forward_01,CHK_META_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded `a_data` with the requester's. Any changed bit of a write fails
it.

|Size unchanged (`REQ_META_02e`) |_legal request forwarded_ (<<chk_meta_forward_01,CHK_META_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded `a_size` with the requester's. A changed size fails it.

|Byte mask unchanged (`REQ_META_02f`) |_legal request forwarded_ (<<chk_meta_forward_01,CHK_META_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded `a_mask` with the requester's. A byte added or dropped fails it.

|User bits unchanged (`REQ_META_02g`) |_legal request forwarded_ (<<chk_meta_forward_01,CHK_META_FORWARD_01>>)
|The check compares the forwarded `a_user`, its command and data integrity included, with the
requester's. Any changed bit fails it.

|No request invented (`REQ_META_08`) |_no extra meta SRAM request_ (<<chk_meta_forward_02,CHK_META_FORWARD_02>>)
|A request on `meta_sram_tl` with no legal request presented behind it matches nothing and fails
the check.

|Same cycle when alone (`REQ_META_14`) |_legal request forwarded_ (<<chk_meta_forward_01,CHK_META_FORWARD_01>>)
|While no other port presents a request, the check requires the request on `meta_sram_tl` in the
very cycle it is presented. One cycle late fails it.
|===

*Cases:* _legal Get_, a legal `Get` accepted on port `i`, one cover per port; _legal Put_, a legal
`PutFullData` on port `i`, one cover per port; _two ports at once_, _three ports at once_ and _four
ports at once_, two, three and four ports presenting legal requests in one cycle.

*Edge cases:* _region first word_ and _region last word_, the first and last word of port
`i`{empty}'s region, one cover each per port: `0x1100_0000` and `0x1100_0BFC` on the bitmap ports
(0, 2, 3), `0x1100_0C00` and `0x1100_97FC` on the tag port (1).

*Never:* a request on `meta_sram_tl` that no port presented; a forwarded request with a changed
address, opcode, size, mask, data or integrity.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* the open decision on refused requests at a port (decision D28 of the
checker 2 uarch;
a finding): whether the same-cycle
part of _legal request forwarded_ also holds for a legal request presented while a refused request
of its own port is still unanswered. Question an open question, for _legal request
forwarded_ on a `PutFullData` from `corerevbm_tl` or the engine's bitmap port: the check takes the
legality rule as written.

'''

[[tp_meta_refuse]]
==== meta_refuse: an illegal request is answered with an error, never forwarded

*Rule:* a refused request never reaches `meta_sram_tl`. It is answered exactly once, with `d_error`
set and a valid response integrity, and for a `Get` a valid data integrity.

*Observed at:* the four requester ports and `meta_sram_tl`.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_meta_refuse_01]]`CHK_META_REFUSE_01` |in own region |backward |Every request on `meta_sram_tl` lies in the region of the port it came
from, the input named in the two lowest bits of its `a_source`.
|[[chk_meta_refuse_02]]`CHK_META_REFUSE_02` |only in CHERIoT mode |backward |Every request on `meta_sram_tl` comes in CHERIoT mode (`Ena`).
|[[chk_meta_refuse_03]]`CHK_META_REFUSE_03` |only full words |backward |Every request on `meta_sram_tl` is a full word (`FullWord`).
|[[chk_meta_refuse_04]]`CHK_META_REFUSE_04` |only Get or PutFullData |backward |Every request on `meta_sram_tl` is a `Get` or a `PutFullData`.
|[[chk_meta_refuse_05]]`CHK_META_REFUSE_05` |illegal request gets error |forward |The answer to a refused request carries `d_error`.
|[[chk_meta_refuse_06]]`CHK_META_REFUSE_06` |error answer carries valid integrity |forward |The answer to a refused request carries a valid
response integrity and, for a `Get`, a valid data integrity.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|No request outside its port's region (`REQ_META_03`) |_in own region_ (<<chk_meta_refuse_01,CHK_META_REFUSE_01>>)
|The check reads the port from the forwarded source ID and compares the address with that port's
region. A bitmap port reaching a tag word, or the tag port reaching the bitmap, fails it.

|No request outside CHERIoT mode (`REQ_META_04`) |_only in CHERIoT mode_ (<<chk_meta_refuse_02,CHK_META_REFUSE_02>>)
|The check fails on any request on `meta_sram_tl` while the mode enable is not `MuBi4True`. The
cases try a strict `MuBi4False` and an invalid encoding.

|Only full aligned words (`REQ_META_05`) |_only full words_ (<<chk_meta_refuse_03,CHK_META_REFUSE_03>>)
|The check fails on any request on `meta_sram_tl` that is not a full word at a word-aligned
address. A forwarded one- or two-byte `Get` fails it.

|Only `Get` or `PutFullData` (`REQ_META_06`) |_only Get or PutFullData_ (<<chk_meta_refuse_04,CHK_META_REFUSE_04>>)
|The check fails on any other opcode on `meta_sram_tl`. A forwarded `PutPartialData` fails it.

|Refused request answered (`REQ_META_07a`) |`meta_flow` _request eventually answered_ (<<chk_meta_flow_03,CHK_META_FLOW_03>>)
|That check covers every accepted request, refused ones included. The tool looks for a run where a
refused request is never answered; finding one fails it.

|Refused request answered at most once (`REQ_META_07b`) |`meta_flow` _no extra answer_ (<<chk_meta_flow_02,CHK_META_FLOW_02>>)
|An answer must name a request outstanding on its port (the TL-UL rules on each requester port). A
second error answer to one request names none and fails the check.

|Error answer has `d_error` (`REQ_META_07c`) |_illegal request gets error_ (<<chk_meta_refuse_05,CHK_META_REFUSE_05>>)
|The check looks at the answer to every refused request. An answer with `d_error` at 0 fails it.

|Error answer's response integrity (`REQ_META_16a`) |_error answer carries valid integrity_ (<<chk_meta_refuse_06,CHK_META_REFUSE_06>>)
|The check recomputes the response integrity of every error answer. A broken one fails it: a denial
software can cause must not become an integrity fault at the requester.

|Error answer's data integrity for a `Get` (`REQ_META_16b`) |_error answer carries valid integrity_ (<<chk_meta_refuse_06,CHK_META_REFUSE_06>>)
|The check recomputes the data integrity of the error answer to every refused `Get`. A broken one
fails it.
|===

.Truth table: the four conditions, one cover per row and per port (64 covers)
[cols="1,1,1,1,4",options="header"]
|===
|`Ena` |In region |Full word |`Get` or `PutFullData` |Result, decided by

|1 |1 |1 |1 |forwarded: `meta_forward` _legal request forwarded_
(<<chk_meta_forward_01,CHK_META_FORWARD_01>>)
|any other combination (15 rows) | | | |refused: not forwarded, by the check of each broken
condition (<<chk_meta_refuse_01,CHK_META_REFUSE_01>> to
<<chk_meta_refuse_04,CHK_META_REFUSE_04>>); `d_error`, by _illegal request gets error_
(<<chk_meta_refuse_05,CHK_META_REFUSE_05>>)
|===

The _truth table row_ covers: one per row `r` and port `i`, with `r` read from the four columns as
bits, `Ena` the most significant: row 15 is the forwarded one.

.Cases: one condition broken from a legal request, each refused
[cols="2,1,4",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Broken |Request

|ePMP mode |mode |`cheriot_ena_i` = `MuBi4False`
|invalid mode |mode |an invalid `cheriot_ena_i` value such as `4'h0`
|tag port reads bitmap |region |tag port reads `0x1100_0100` (the bitmap)
|software reads tag word |region |`revbm_tl_d` reads `0x1100_8C48` (a tag word)
|outside the meta SRAM |region |any port, `0x1100_9800` (the meta SRAM top) and `0x10FF_FFFC`
(below the base)
|sub-word Get |size |a `Get` of one byte (`a_size` = 0) and of two bytes (`a_size` = 1)
|partial Put |opcode |a `PutPartialData` of all four bytes
|===

*Edge cases:* _bitmap last word_ and _tag first word_, the region seam seen from each port `i`, one
cover each per port: a full-word `Get` of `0x1100_0BFC`, legal on the bitmap ports and illegal on
the tag port; of `0x1100_0C00`, the reverse. _Late answer_, one cover per port: a refused request
on port `i` answered a cycle or more after it was taken: _illegal request gets error_ seen on an
answer that waited.

*Never:* an illegal request on `meta_sram_tl`; an illegal request with no answer or two; an
illegal request answered without `d_error`.

*Run:* V1. The requests on every requester port are free, so illegal ones are reached. The TL-UL
host rules (assumption A8) already exclude a word-unaligned full-word access
(`addrSizeAligned`) and undefined opcodes, so a request refused only for its alignment is
unreachable; the alignment condition is reached through sub-word sizes.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for _error answer carries valid integrity_.
Question an open question, for the truth table of a `PutFullData` from `corerevbm_tl` or the
engine's bitmap port: the checks take the legality rule as written.

'''

[[tp_meta_return]]
==== meta_return: each answer to its own requester, unchanged

*Rule:* an answer on `meta_sram_tl` reaches only the answer's input, in the cycle it arrives, with
the returned source ID as `d_source` and every other D-channel field unchanged. The meta SRAM's
answer is taken exactly when that port takes it.

*Observed at:* the four requester ports and `meta_sram_tl`.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_meta_return_01]]`CHK_META_RETURN_01` |answer to its port |forward |An answer on `meta_sram_tl` is presented in the same
cycle at the port of the input named in the two lowest bits of its `d_source`.
|[[chk_meta_return_02]]`CHK_META_RETURN_02` |source shifted back |forward |At that port, the answer's `d_source` is the `meta_sram_tl`
answer's `d_source` shifted right by two.
|[[chk_meta_return_03]]`CHK_META_RETURN_03` |fields unchanged |forward |That answer carries every other D-channel field unchanged; `d_data`
only in an `AccessAckData`, the one answer that carries data ([TLUL]).
|[[chk_meta_return_04]]`CHK_META_RETURN_04` |taken with its port |forward |The meta SRAM's answer is taken exactly when its port takes it.
|[[chk_meta_return_05]]`CHK_META_RETURN_05` |only the meta SRAM's answer |backward |The answer a port gets to a legal request is the meta SRAM's
answer to it, in the same cycle: no port gets an answer the meta SRAM did not send it.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Answer reaches its requester (`REQ_META_09a`) |_answer to its port_ (<<chk_meta_return_01,CHK_META_RETURN_01>>), _taken with its port_ (<<chk_meta_return_04,CHK_META_RETURN_04>>)
|The first check requires the answer at the input its source ID names, the second that the meta
SRAM's answer is taken only when that port takes it. A dropped answer, or one taken before its
port takes it, fails one of them.

|Answer reaches no other port (`REQ_META_09b`) |_only the meta SRAM's answer_ (<<chk_meta_return_05,CHK_META_RETURN_05>>)
|A port that gets an answer must find the meta SRAM sending one to it in that cycle. An answer
copied to a second port, or sent to the wrong one, finds none there and fails the check.

|Requester's source ID returned (`REQ_META_10`) |_source shifted back_ (<<chk_meta_return_02,CHK_META_RETURN_02>>)
|The check compares the answer's `d_source` with the meta SRAM's shifted right by two. With the
meta SRAM returning the forwarded source ID, that is the requester's own `a_source`; a wrong shift
fails it.

|Answer's opcode (`REQ_META_11a`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_meta_return_03,CHK_META_RETURN_03>>)
|The check compares the answer's `d_opcode` with the meta SRAM's. A changed opcode fails it.

|Answer's error (`REQ_META_11b`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_meta_return_03,CHK_META_RETURN_03>>)
|The check compares the answer's `d_error` with the meta SRAM's. An error dropped or added fails
it.

|Answer's param (`REQ_META_11c`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_meta_return_03,CHK_META_RETURN_03>>)
|The check compares the answer's `d_param` with the meta SRAM's. Any changed bit fails it.

|Answer's size (`REQ_META_11d`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_meta_return_03,CHK_META_RETURN_03>>)
|The check compares the answer's `d_size` with the meta SRAM's. A changed size fails it.

|Answer's data (`REQ_META_11e`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_meta_return_03,CHK_META_RETURN_03>>)
|The check compares `d_data` in every `AccessAckData` with the meta SRAM's. Any changed data bit
fails it.

|Answer's sink ID (`REQ_META_11f`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_meta_return_03,CHK_META_RETURN_03>>)
|The check compares the answer's `d_sink` with the meta SRAM's. A changed ID fails it.

|Answer's user bits (`REQ_META_11g`) |_fields unchanged_ (<<chk_meta_return_03,CHK_META_RETURN_03>>)
|The check compares the answer's `d_user`, its response and data integrity included, with the meta
SRAM's. Any changed bit fails it.

|Answer in the cycle it arrives (`REQ_META_15`) |_answer to its port_ (<<chk_meta_return_01,CHK_META_RETURN_01>>)
|The check requires the answer at its port in the very cycle it arrives on `meta_sram_tl`. One
cycle late fails it.
|===

*Cases:* _answer to each port_, an answer to port `i`, one cover per port; _ports back to back_,
answers in consecutive cycles to different ports; _worked example_, `0x56` returns to port 2 as
`0x15`; _late answer_, one cover per port: a legal request on port `i` answered a cycle or more
after it was taken: _only the meta SRAM's answer_ seen on an answer that waited.

*Edge cases:* _source top bits_, a returned `d_source` of `0x3F`, every bit a port may use (the top
two bits stay free, assumption A9); _error answer_, an answer with `d_error`;
_bad response integrity_, an answer with a broken response integrity. Both pass unchanged.

*Never:* an answer at the wrong port or at two ports; a changed `d_data`, `d_error` or integrity.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for _source shifted back_: the check takes the top
bits of each requester's `a_source` to stay free.

'''

[[tp_meta_flow]]
==== meta_flow: round robin, every request answered

*Rule:* round robin ([TLUL] `tlul_socket_m1`: "Requests coming from each host ports are arbitrated
in the socket based on round-robin scheme"): while a request waits at a host port of the 4:1
arbiter, a checked stream, at most three requests of the other host ports are forwarded before it.
A request presented on a requester port is accepted unless the requester withdraws or changes it
first, and every accepted request is answered exactly once, given the meta SRAM accepts and answers
and the requesters take their answers. A changed request is a new one: TileLink guarantees
acceptance only for "presented beats", held unchanged "until ready is also HIGH" ([TL] §5.1, p29).

*Observed at:* the 4:1 arbiter's four host ports and `meta_sram_tl` for _round robin bound_; the
four requester ports for the other checks.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_meta_flow_01]]`CHK_META_FLOW_01` |round robin bound |safety |The bounded form of round robin, at the arbiter's host ports: at most three
grants to the other inputs while a request waits. It needs no fairness assumption.
|[[chk_meta_flow_02]]`CHK_META_FLOW_02` |no extra answer |safety |No request is answered twice: an answer only to an outstanding request
(xref:{tp}#tp_tlul_protocol[`tlul_protocol`] _TL-UL rules hold_ on each requester port).
|[[chk_meta_flow_03]]`CHK_META_FLOW_03` |request eventually answered |liveness |Every accepted request is answered in the end.
|[[chk_meta_flow_04]]`CHK_META_FLOW_04` |request eventually accepted |liveness |A request presented on a requester port is accepted in the end,
unless the requester withdraws or changes it first.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Held request accepted in the end (`REQ_META_12`) |_round robin bound_ (<<chk_meta_flow_01,CHK_META_FLOW_01>>), _request eventually accepted_ (<<chk_meta_flow_04,CHK_META_FLOW_04>>)
|At the arbiter, a request waits through at most three other grants, so it is granted while the
meta SRAM keeps accepting. At the port, the tool looks for a run where a held request waits for
ever while the meta SRAM keeps accepting; finding one fails _request eventually accepted_.

|Accepted request answered (`REQ_META_13a`) |_request eventually answered_ (<<chk_meta_flow_03,CHK_META_FLOW_03>>)
|The tool looks for a run where an accepted request is never answered while the meta SRAM answers
and the requesters take their answers. Finding one fails the check.

|Answered at most once (`REQ_META_13b`) |_no extra answer_ (<<chk_meta_flow_02,CHK_META_FLOW_02>>)
|An answer must name a request outstanding on its port. A second answer to one request names none
and fails the check.
|===

*Cases:* _all four present_, all four host ports of the arbiter presenting in one cycle; _waits for
three_, one cover per input `i`: input `i` waits while the other three are granted, one each, then
is granted itself.

*Never:* a request at a host port of the arbiter passed over by a fourth grant to the others; an
accepted request answered twice, or never; a request held on a requester port never accepted while
the meta SRAM accepts and answers and the requester takes its answers.

*Run:* _round robin bound_ and _no extra answer_ in V1. _Request eventually accepted_ in the
liveness A run, which assumes only `REQ_META_12`{empty}'s own condition, that the meta SRAM keeps
accepting. _Request eventually answered_ in the liveness B run: the neighbours never hang
(assumption A10), the meta SRAM answers a cycle or more after each request, in
order, held until taken (assumption A16), and the RMW filter and the engine's
bitmap port take every answer offered (contracts C4 and C5; decisions D35 and D36 of the
checker 2 uarch). The
xref:{tp}#run_variants[run variants] name the Jasper task of each.

*Blocked by:* the open decision on refused requests at a port (decision D28 of the
checker 2 uarch;
a finding), for
`REQ_META_12`{empty}'s condition: a legal request waits while a refused request of its own port is
unanswered, so the requester must also take its answers. Question an open question, for the
two liveness checks.

=== Tag path end to end

How the access checker guards the tag regions:
xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc#tag_sharing[design architecture doc, Sharing
the meta SRAM].

.Testpoints of the tag path
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_tag_isolation,tag_isolation>> |Only the tag port reaches the tag regions, and only in CHERIoT mode; the three bitmap ports never reach them.
|===

[[tp_tag_isolation]]
==== tag_isolation: the tag store is reached only by the tag path

*Rule:* a request from the tag port reaches `meta_sram_tl` only inside `0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF`
and only in CHERIoT mode; a request from the other three ports never reaches that range. These are
the tag path's part of `REQ_META_03` and `REQ_META_04` (`meta_refuse` _in own region_ and _only in
CHERIoT mode_), kept as their own requirements because they carry the countermeasure
`MEM.SW_NOACCESS` ("The capability tag store is not memory mapped").

*Observed at:* `meta_sram_tl`; the requester ports for the covers.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tag_isolation_01]]`CHK_TAG_ISOLATION_01` |tag port in tag regions |backward |A request on `meta_sram_tl` from the tag port lies in
`0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF`.
|[[chk_tag_isolation_02]]`CHK_TAG_ISOLATION_02` |tag port only in CHERIoT mode |backward |A request on `meta_sram_tl` from the tag port comes only in
CHERIoT mode.
|[[chk_tag_isolation_03]]`CHK_TAG_ISOLATION_03` |other ports never reach tags |backward |A request on `meta_sram_tl` from any other port lies outside
`0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF`.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Tag path reaches only the tag regions (`REQ_TAG_05`) |_tag port in tag regions_ (<<chk_tag_isolation_01,CHK_TAG_ISOLATION_01>>)
|The check reads the port from the forwarded source ID and fails on a tag port request outside
`0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF`. A tag port request reaching the bitmap fails it.

|No tag path access outside CHERIoT mode (`REQ_TAG_06`) |_tag port only in CHERIoT mode_ (<<chk_tag_isolation_02,CHK_TAG_ISOLATION_02>>)
|The check fails on any tag port request on `meta_sram_tl` while the mode enable is not
`MuBi4True`. The cases try all 16 mode values.

|Other ports never reach the tags (`REQ_TAG_11`) |_other ports never reach tags_ (<<chk_tag_isolation_03,CHK_TAG_ISOLATION_03>>)
|The check fails on any request from ports 0, 2 or 3 inside `0x1100_0C00`-`0x1100_97FF`. Software
reading a tag word through `revbm_tl_d` fails it.
|===

*Cases:* _every mode value_, a request taken on the tag port in each of the 16 `cheriot_ena_i`
values, one cover per value; _software at first tag word_, _software at middle tag word_ and
_software at last tag word_, `revbm_tl_d` at `0x1100_0C00`, `0x1100_8C48`, `0x1100_97FC`; _core
TRVK at tag word_, `corerevbm_tl` at `0x1100_0C00`; _engine at tag word_, the engine's bitmap port
at `0x1100_0C00`.

*Never:* a tag-region address on `meta_sram_tl` that came from a bitmap port; any tag port request
on `meta_sram_tl` in ePMP mode; a tag port request on `meta_sram_tl` outside the tag regions.

*Run:* V1.

[[checker3]]
== Checker 3: revocation engine


[[c3_terms]]
=== Terms

The request and address terms shared with the other checkers (CHERIoT mode, `Get`, full word,
tagged region and its top, malformed, integrity ok and the like) are in the xref:{tp}#terms[main
testplan, Terms]; the tag word and tag bit of an address are in the
xref:{tp1}#_terms[checker 1 testplan, Terms]. Source tags are
those of the checker 3 requirements doc.

[cols="2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Term |Meaning

|Capability |64 bits and a tag. W0, the word at the 8-byte-aligned address, holds its address `a`;
W1, the word 4 bytes above, its metadata: `R` (bit 31, reserved), `p` (30:25, the compressed
permissions), `otype` (24:22, the object type), `E` (21:18, the exponent), `T` (17:9, the top
field) and `B` (8:0, the base field) ([ISA] §7.3 and §7.12, Figure 7.2, PDF page 62). A capability
store writes the low word, then the high word. The testbench decodes the base and the permissions
from the ISA, never with an RTL function.
|Sealed |`otype` is not 0. A sealed capability of a memory format is not a sealing capability, so
it is revoked like any other ([ISA] §7.13.2: "0 unsealed ... 9-15 non-executable capability sealed
with given otype"; the CLC exemption tests the permissions only).
|Base |The decoded base of a capability, from `a`, `E` and `B`, in the four steps of
<<base_steps>> ([ISA] §7.13.3, PDF pages 69-70; Sail `getCapBoundsBits`, PDF pages 149-150). Every
bit pattern decodes: the ISA gives no rule for a tagged capability with malformed bounds ([ISA] PDF
pages 70, 154-155), so the engine is checked on the decoded base alone.
|Sealing capability |A capability whose permissions are in the sealing format and grant SE, US or
U0: `Sealing = (p[4:3] == 0) and (p[2:0] != 0)` ([ISA] CLC, PDF page 114, Sail: `let isSealingCap
== cr.permit_seal \| cr.permit_unseal \| cr.perm_user0`). Every permission format: <<perm_formats>>.
|Revocable base |A base in the main SRAM region, `0x1000_0000` up to `0x1003_0000` ([PG]: "capabilities whose base lies outside the main SRAM region are never revoked").
|Revocation word and bit |Of a revocable base: bit `((base - 0x1000_0000) >> 3) & 31` of the bitmap
word `0x1100_0000 + 4 * ((base - 0x1000_0000) >> 8)` ([ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map, `revbm` window).
A base anywhere in an 8-byte granule uses that granule's bit, the granule being `base & ~7` ([ISA]
CLC Sail: `align_down(log2_revocation_granule_size, base)`, granule size 8). The engine uses the
bit of the base, never of the address ([ISA] §7.8: "the revocation bit corresponding to the base
address of the capability (N.B. not the address)").
|Revoked |A swept capability is revoked when it is tagged, is not a sealing capability, has a
revocable base, and its base's revocation bit is set or its lookup failed ([ToO] Revocation
Engine; [PG]). Its tag is the tag the engine's tag filter returns with its words. Its bit is set
when the word its lookup returned has its base's revocation bit set. Its lookup failed when it was
answered with `d_error`, failed the integrity check or was malformed.
|A capability's lookup |The lookup presented on the bitmap port while the TRVK filter holds the
capability's W1 answer, from its arrival on the TRVK filter's downstream port until its departure
on the engine's read port. The TRVK filter decodes the base from both words, so it can look the
bit up only once W1's answer has reached it, and it applies the load barrier to that answer before
it passes it on. A DV reading (question an open question).
|Start write |With the register file a blackbox, software writing 1 to `TBRE_START` is the
register file's write strobe for `TBRE_START` with the value 1. The register file's outputs follow
the register file model (contract C20 of the TB architecture).
|Set request |What the engine writes into a field of the register file (`TBRE_STATUS.start_err`, `sweep_err`, `INTR_STATE.tbre_done`): the field's write enable with the value 1. The busy field is
what the engine last wrote into it; its storage is the register file's. `TBRE_REGWEN` and
`TBRE_EPOCH` are `hwext` registers ([HJSON]): software reads what the engine drives, so the checks
read them directly.
|Taken start |A start write while `TBRE_REGWEN` is 1, in CHERIoT mode, with `NUM` not 0 and `BASE`
in a tagged region ([ToO]: "starts a sweep ... if").
|Ignored start |Any other start write while `TBRE_REGWEN` is 1 ([ToO]: "Any other start is ignored").
|BASE, NUM |`TBRE_BASE_ADDR` (bits 2:0 read as 0) and `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` at the start ([HJSON]).
|N, swept capabilities |`N = min(NUM, (top - BASE) / 8)`, with top the exclusive top of the tagged
region of `BASE`; the swept capabilities are `BASE + 8k` for `0 \<= k < N` ([ToO]: "the engine
sweeps `min(TBRE_NUM_CAPS, (top - TBRE_BASE_ADDR) / 8)` capabilities"). Worked numbers:
<<n_numbers>>.
|Active |`TBRE_REGWEN` is 0 ([ToO]: "While the engine is active ... `TBRE_REGWEN` is low").
|Resolved |Proposed: both words of the capability read and answered, its lookup answered, its
clear answered (question an open question).
|Tracked capability |One swept capability, `BASE + 8k` with `k < N`, which the tool chooses at the
start; any `k` may be chosen, so a check on it covers every swept capability. Its tracking phases
run from `TrkIdle` to `TrkResolved`.
|Read port, clear port |The engine presents its reads on its read port, in front of its TRVK
filter, and its clears on its clear port, in front of the socket that merges them with the TRVK
filter's reads ([ToO]: "a socket merges its downstream port with the engine's tag clears in front
of the tag filter"). The TRVK filter and the socket can hold a read or a clear for a cycle or more,
so the windows below start and end at these ports, not at `tbre_tl_h` or the arbiter (DV reading,
question an open question).
|Watch window |Of a capability: from the cycle the read of its W0 is presented on the read port
until the cycle before its clear is presented on the clear port ([ToO]: "The watch starts when
...").
|Stale window, held |From the cycle the capability's clear is presented on the clear port until
the cycle before it reaches the RMW filter. From the cycle it reaches the RMW filter until it is
accepted, the clear is held ([ToO]: "From the presentation of the clear until it reaches the RMW
filter"; "Once the clear is at the RMW filter ... holds it there"; checker 3 uarch).
|Touch |A core write touches a capability when it is presented on `cored_tl_d`, or accepted there
and not yet answered, with its address in the capability's 8 bytes ([ToO]: "every write the core
presents ... and every write it accepted there until the write is answered"; "at capability
granularity").
|===

[[base_steps]]
.Base, step by step
[cols="1,4,3",options="header"]
|===
|Step |Formula |Sail, verbatim

|1 |`e = 24` if `E == 15`, else `e = E` |`let E = if c.cE == 0xf then cap_max_E_bits`
|2 |`a_mid = (a >> e) & 0x1FF`; `a_top = a >> (e + 9)` |`let a_mid = truncate(a >> E, cap_mantissa_width)`
|3 |`c_b = -1` if `a_mid < B`, else `c_b = 0` |`let a_hi = if a_mid <_u c.B then 1 else 0`; `let
c_b = 0 - a_hi`
|4 |`Base = (((a_top + c_b) << (e + 9)) \| (B << e)) mod 2^32^` |`let base : CapAddrBits =
truncate((a_top + c_b) @ c.B @ zeros(E), cap_addr_width)`
|===

.Base, worked numbers computed from the steps
[cols="3,2,2,2,2",options="header"]
|===
|Capability |W0 (`a`) |W1 |`E`, `B`, `c_b` |Base

|64-byte object, address 16 bytes in |`0x1000_4010` |`0x7E00_8000` |0, `0x000`, 0 |`0x1000_4000`
|64-byte object across a 512-byte line, address before the line |`0x1000_41F8` |`0x7E00_61F0` |0,
`0x1F0`, 0 |`0x1000_41F0`
|the same object, address after the line |`0x1000_4210` |`0x7E00_61F0` |0, `0x1F0`, -1
|`0x1000_41F0`
|object with 16-byte granular bounds |`0x1000_4100` |`0x7E10_4000` |4, `0x000`, 0 |`0x1000_4000`
|root capability |`0x0000_0000` |`0x7E3E_0000` |15, `0x000`, 0 |`0x0000_0000`
|===

The second and third rows are one capability: the correction `c_b` gives the same base from two
addresses. The base `0x1000_41F0` has revocation bit 30 of word `0x1100_0104`; the address
`0x1000_4210` lies in another granule, bit 2 of word `0x1100_0108`. Revocation follows the base.

[[perm_formats]]
.Permission formats and the sealing capability ([ISA] Figure 7.4, PDF page 65)
[cols="2,3,1,4",options="header"]
|===
|`p` (bits 5:0) |Format |Sealing |Note

|`G 11xxx` |memory, capability read-write |0 |`G` is the global bit; it never matters here
|`G 101xx` |memory, capability read-only |0 |
|`G 10000` |memory, capability write-only |0 |
|`G 100xx`, `xx` not `00` |memory, data only |0 |
|`G 01xxx` |executable |0 |
|`G 00` U0 SE US, not all 0 |sealing |1 |any one of U0, SE, US is enough
|`G 00000` |no permissions, in the sealing format |0 |gap: question an open question
([ISA] §7.13.8: "may also behave unexpectedly with respect to revocation")
|===
