=== Start, status and interrupt

How the revocation engine works:
xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc#revocation[design architecture doc, the meta
SRAM and revocation].

.Testpoints of the start, status and interrupt
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_tbre_start,tbre_start>> |A taken start makes the engine active; an ignored start moves nothing and sets `start_err`, which nothing else sets.
|<<tp_tbre_status,tbre_status>> |`TBRE_REGWEN` is low from the cycle after a taken start until the sweep is resolved, busy follows it one cycle later and the epoch's active bit is its inverse.
|<<tp_tbre_epoch,tbre_epoch>> |The epoch count steps by one when a sweep without an error ends, and at no other time.
|<<tp_tbre_intr,tbre_intr>> |`tbre_done` is set when a sweep ends or software tests it, and only then; the interrupt line follows the enabled state.
|===

[[tp_tbre_start]]
==== tbre_start: which starts start a sweep

*Rule:* a taken start starts a sweep over the swept capabilities. An ignored start starts nothing,
leaves `TBRE_STATUS.busy`, `TBRE_REGWEN` and `TBRE_EPOCH` unchanged and sets `start_err`;
`start_err` is set by nothing else. That `start_err` stays set, that locked writes have no effect
and that the registers keep their values is register file behaviour, checked in the main
testplan's xref:{tp}#tp_csr[csr].

*Observed at:* the register file's outputs (`TBRE_START`, `TBRE_BASE_ADDR`, `TBRE_NUM_CAPS`), the
engine's writes into `TBRE_STATUS`, `TBRE_REGWEN`, `TBRE_EPOCH`.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tbre_start_01]]`CHK_TBRE_START_01` |taken start activates |forward |A taken start makes the engine active: `TBRE_REGWEN`
is 0 in the next cycle. The same obligation as `tbre_status` _REGWEN low after start_
(<<chk_tbre_status_01,CHK_TBRE_STATUS_01>>).
|[[chk_tbre_start_02]]`CHK_TBRE_START_02` |REGWEN falls only on start |backward |`TBRE_REGWEN` falls only in the cycle after a taken start,
so an ignored start starts no sweep.
|[[chk_tbre_start_03]]`CHK_TBRE_START_03` |ignored start changes nothing |stable |In the cycle after an ignored start, `TBRE_REGWEN` is
still 1, `TBRE_EPOCH` is as before and the busy field is 0: the start moves none of them. Busy is
0, not "as before": when the start comes in the cycle a sweep ends, busy falls then, as
`tbre_status` _busy follows REGWEN_ (<<chk_tbre_status_03,CHK_TBRE_STATUS_03>>) requires (checker
3 uarch).
|[[chk_tbre_start_04]]`CHK_TBRE_START_04` |ignored start sets error |forward |An ignored start is followed by a `start_err` set request,
at some point; the spec gives no bound (premise P7).
|[[chk_tbre_start_05]]`CHK_TBRE_START_05` |error set next cycle |forward |That set request comes no later than the cycle after the
ignored start, so the first register read after the start sees it. A DV reading (question
an open question).
|[[chk_tbre_start_06]]`CHK_TBRE_START_06` |error only after ignored start |backward |A `start_err` set request comes only while an ignored
start has not had one yet: a one-bit credit.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|A taken start starts a sweep (`REQ_TBRE_01`) |_taken start activates_ (<<chk_tbre_start_01,CHK_TBRE_START_01>>), _REGWEN falls only on start_ (<<chk_tbre_start_02,CHK_TBRE_START_02>>)
|The first check requires the engine active in the cycle after every taken start, the second lets
it become active only then. A design that drops a taken start keeps `TBRE_REGWEN` at 1 and fails
the first. Which words the sweep reads is `tbre_sweep`{empty}'s.

|An ignored start starts no sweep (`REQ_TBRE_02a`) |_REGWEN falls only on start_ (<<chk_tbre_start_02,CHK_TBRE_START_02>>)
|`TBRE_REGWEN` may fall only in the cycle after a taken start. A sweep started by an ignored start
drops it with no taken start before and fails the check.

|An ignored start leaves busy unchanged (`REQ_TBRE_02b`) |_ignored start changes nothing_ (<<chk_tbre_start_03,CHK_TBRE_START_03>>)
|The check requires the busy field 0 in the cycle after an ignored start, which only comes while
the engine is idle. A busy field raised by the start fails it.

|An ignored start leaves `TBRE_REGWEN` unchanged (`REQ_TBRE_02c`) |_ignored start changes nothing_ (<<chk_tbre_start_03,CHK_TBRE_START_03>>)
|The check requires `TBRE_REGWEN` still 1 in the cycle after an ignored start. A fall fails it.

|An ignored start leaves the epoch unchanged (`REQ_TBRE_02d`) |_ignored start changes nothing_ (<<chk_tbre_start_03,CHK_TBRE_START_03>>)
|The check compares `TBRE_EPOCH` after an ignored start with its value before. Any change fails
it.

|An ignored start sets `start_err` (`REQ_TBRE_03`) |_ignored start sets error_ (<<chk_tbre_start_04,CHK_TBRE_START_04>>), _error set next cycle_ (<<chk_tbre_start_05,CHK_TBRE_START_05>>)
|The first check looks for a run where an ignored start never gets its set request; the second
requires it by the next cycle, so the first read after the start sees it (DV reading, question
an open question). A design that skips or delays the set fails one of them.

|Only an ignored start sets `start_err` (`REQ_TBRE_04a`) |_error only after ignored start_ (<<chk_tbre_start_06,CHK_TBRE_START_06>>)
|Each ignored start gives one credit, and its set request uses it up. A set request after a taken
start, or a second one for one ignored start, finds no credit and fails the check.
|===

.Truth table: the three start conditions, with `TBRE_REGWEN` = 1 (rule R1 of contract C20); one cover per row
[cols="1,1,1,2",options="header"]
|===
|CHERIoT mode |`NUM` not 0 |`BASE` in a tagged region |Result

|1 |1 |1 |sweep starts
|1 |1 |0 |ignored, `start_err`
|1 |0 |1 |ignored, `start_err`
|1 |0 |0 |ignored, `start_err`
|0 |1 |1 |ignored, `start_err`
|0 |1 |0 |ignored, `start_err`
|0 |0 |1 |ignored, `start_err`
|0 |0 |0 |ignored, `start_err`
|===

Each row is one cover of the _truth table row_ family: 8 covers. The first row is decided by _taken
start activates_; the others by _REGWEN falls only on start_, _ignored start changes nothing_ and
_ignored start sets error_.

.Cases: one input varied from a taken start (`BASE` = `0x1000_0000`, `NUM` = 1, CHERIoT mode)
[cols="2,2,3,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Varied |Value |Result

|NVM base |`BASE` |`0x3000_0000` (NVM) |starts
|last SRAM capability |`BASE` |`0x1002_FFF8` (last main SRAM capability) |starts, `N` = 1
|SRAM top |`BASE` |`0x1003_0000` (main SRAM top) |ignored
|below SRAM |`BASE` |`0x0FFF_FFF8` |ignored
|below NVM |`BASE` |`0x2FFF_FFF8` |ignored
|NVM top |`BASE` |`0x3020_0000` (NVM top) |ignored
|meta SRAM base |`BASE` |`0x1100_0000` (meta SRAM) |ignored
|peripheral base |`BASE` |`0x4000_0000` (a peripheral) |ignored
|zero capabilities |`NUM` |0 |ignored
|largest NUM |`NUM` |`0x7FFF_FFFF` |starts; `N` clipped (<<tp_tbre_sweep>>)
|ePMP mode |mode |`MuBi4False` |ignored
|invalid mode |mode |an invalid `cheriot_ena_i`, `4'h0` |ignored
|===

*Edge cases:* _write of 0_, a write of 0 to `TBRE_START`: nothing happens; _same range again_, a
second start after a sweep, with no register write between: the same range is swept again; _error
again_, an ignored start while `start_err` is already set: a set request again.

*Never:* a sweep from an ignored start; a `start_err` set request after a taken start; an ignored
start that moves `TBRE_REGWEN`, busy or the epoch.

*Run:* V1 and V4, with the register file blackboxed and its outputs following the register file
model (contract C20).

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for _error set next cycle_.

'''

[[tp_tbre_status]]
==== tbre_status: active, busy and the first read

*Rule:* `TBRE_REGWEN` falls in the cycle after a taken start and stays 0 until every swept
capability is resolved; it is 1 at all other times. In every cycle, the busy field equals the
inverse of `TBRE_REGWEN` one cycle earlier, and `TBRE_EPOCH.active` the inverse of `TBRE_REGWEN` in
the same cycle.

*Observed at:* `TBRE_REGWEN`, the engine's writes of `TBRE_STATUS.busy`, `TBRE_EPOCH`; the engine's
ports, for what is still outstanding.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tbre_status_01]]`CHK_TBRE_STATUS_01` |REGWEN low after start |forward |`TBRE_REGWEN` is 0 in the cycle after a taken start.
|[[chk_tbre_status_02]]`CHK_TBRE_STATUS_02` |REGWEN rises only when resolved |backward |`TBRE_REGWEN` rises only when the tracked capability
of the sweep is resolved and no read, lookup or clear of the engine is outstanding. It uses the
proposed meaning of resolved (question an open question).
|[[chk_tbre_status_03]]`CHK_TBRE_STATUS_03` |busy follows REGWEN |forward |In every cycle, the busy field equals the inverse of
`TBRE_REGWEN` of the cycle before. The busy field is what the engine last wrote into it; its
storage is the register file's (contract C20).
|[[chk_tbre_status_04]]`CHK_TBRE_STATUS_04` |active follows REGWEN |forward |In every cycle, `TBRE_EPOCH.active` equals the inverse of
`TBRE_REGWEN`.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|`TBRE_REGWEN` is 0 from the cycle after a taken start until the sweep is resolved (`REQ_TBRE_07a`) |_REGWEN low after start_ (<<chk_tbre_status_01,CHK_TBRE_STATUS_01>>), _REGWEN rises only when resolved_ (<<chk_tbre_status_02,CHK_TBRE_STATUS_02>>)
|The first check requires the fall in the cycle after the start; the second fails a rise while any
swept capability, the tracked one being any of them, is not yet resolved or anything of the engine
is outstanding. Resolved is a proposed reading (question an open question).

|`TBRE_REGWEN` is 1 at all other times (`REQ_TBRE_07b`) |`tbre_start` _REGWEN falls only on start_ (<<chk_tbre_start_02,CHK_TBRE_START_02>>)
|Outside a sweep, `TBRE_REGWEN` may fall only in the cycle after a taken start, so it stays 1
before a sweep. *Open point:* no check requires the rise once every swept capability is resolved;
`tbre_done` _sweep ends_ (<<chk_tbre_done_01,CHK_TBRE_DONE_01>>) only requires it at some point, and
resolved waits on question an open question.

|Busy is the inverse of `TBRE_REGWEN` one cycle earlier (`REQ_TBRE_08`) |_busy follows REGWEN_ (<<chk_tbre_status_03,CHK_TBRE_STATUS_03>>)
|The check compares the busy field with `TBRE_REGWEN` of the cycle before, in every cycle. A busy
early, late or stuck fails it.

|`TBRE_EPOCH.active` is the inverse of `TBRE_REGWEN` (`REQ_TBRE_09`) |_active follows REGWEN_ (<<chk_tbre_status_04,CHK_TBRE_STATUS_04>>)
|The check compares the two in every cycle. An active bit one cycle off fails it.

|The first read after a taken start sees `TBRE_REGWEN` = 0 (`REQ_TBRE_12a`) |By composition: _REGWEN low after start_ (<<chk_tbre_status_01,CHK_TBRE_STATUS_01>>) and the register interface's request rate (`REQ_REG_02`, main testplan, xref:{tp}#tp_csr[csr])
|The check makes `TBRE_REGWEN` 0 from the cycle after the start. The register interface takes a
request at most every other cycle, so the first read it accepts after the start comes no earlier.

|The first read after a taken start sees the epoch active (`REQ_TBRE_12b`) |By composition: _REGWEN low after start_ (<<chk_tbre_status_01,CHK_TBRE_STATUS_01>>), _active follows REGWEN_ (<<chk_tbre_status_04,CHK_TBRE_STATUS_04>>) and `REQ_REG_02` (main testplan, xref:{tp}#tp_csr[csr])
|The two checks make the epoch odd from the cycle after the start; the request rate keeps the first
read from coming earlier.

|The first read after a taken start sees busy = 1 (`REQ_TBRE_12c`) |By composition: _REGWEN low after start_ (<<chk_tbre_status_01,CHK_TBRE_STATUS_01>>), _busy follows REGWEN_ (<<chk_tbre_status_03,CHK_TBRE_STATUS_03>>) and `REQ_REG_02` (main testplan, xref:{tp}#tp_csr[csr])
|The two checks make busy 1 two cycles after the start write; taking a request at most every other
cycle, the register interface accepts no read before then.
|===

*Cases:* _sweep of one_, a sweep of one capability; _two in flight_, of two, with both words in
flight; _last capability cleared_, one whose last capability needs a clear, so the clear's answer
is the last part to arrive; _each tracking phase_, one cover per phase of the tracked capability,
`TrkIdle` to `TrkResolved`; _tracked first_, _tracked in middle_ and _tracked last_, the tracked
capability first in its sweep, in the middle and last; _reset mid sweep_, a reset in the middle of
a sweep.

*Never:* `TBRE_REGWEN` rising while a read, a lookup or a clear of the sweep is outstanding;
`busy` or `active` out of step.

*Run:* V1 and V4.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for _REGWEN rises only when resolved_: what resolved
means.

'''

[[tp_tbre_epoch]]
==== tbre_epoch: the epoch counts sweeps without an error

*Rule:* in the cycle `TBRE_EPOCH.active` falls, `TBRE_EPOCH.count` steps by one, modulo 2^31^, when
no error cause of <<tp_tbre_errors,tbre_errors>> occurred during that sweep, the cycle `active`
falls included. Otherwise, and in every other cycle, the count keeps its value.

*Observed at:* `TBRE_EPOCH`, and the error causes of <<tp_tbre_errors,tbre_errors>>.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tbre_epoch_01]]`CHK_TBRE_EPOCH_01` |steps unless error |forward |In the cycle `TBRE_EPOCH.active` falls, the count is the old
count plus 1 if no error cause occurred in the sweep, else the old count.
|[[chk_tbre_epoch_02]]`CHK_TBRE_EPOCH_02` |count stable otherwise |stable |In every other cycle, the count is unchanged.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|The count steps when a sweep without an error ends (`REQ_TBRE_10`) |_steps unless error_ (<<chk_tbre_epoch_01,CHK_TBRE_EPOCH_01>>)
|The check computes the expected count from the old one and the causes seen in the sweep. A missed
step, a step of 2 or a wrong wrap fails it.

|The count changes at no other time (`REQ_TBRE_11`) |_steps unless error_ (<<chk_tbre_epoch_01,CHK_TBRE_EPOCH_01>>), _count stable otherwise_ (<<chk_tbre_epoch_02,CHK_TBRE_EPOCH_02>>)
|The first check fails a step at the end of a sweep with an error, the second any change in any
other cycle.
|===

.Cases
[cols="2,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Sweep |`TBRE_EPOCH`

|clean sweep |taken start, no error |4, 5, 6
|read error |taken start, a sweep read answered with `d_error` (no alert) |4, 5, 4
|bitmap error |taken start, a bitmap lookup error (alert) |4, 5, 4
|ignored start |ignored start |4
|ignored after end |an ignored start in the cycle after a sweep ended |6 stays 6
|error left set |`sweep_err` left set by an earlier sweep, this sweep with no error |4, 5, 6:
counted ([ToO]: "A sweep during which any error sets `TBRE_STATUS.sweep_err` is not counted")
|error at end |an error in the cycle `active` clears |4, 5, 4
|===

A start written while the engine is active never reaches the engine (rule R2 of contract C20): its
effect, none, is the CSR testing's (main testplan, xref:{tp}#tp_csr[csr]).

*Edge cases:* _count wraps_, the wrap of the count from 2^31^ - 1 to 0. From reset it takes 2^31^
sweeps, so the run lets the counter start at any value (checker 3 uarch): every value is one
the counter reaches after enough sweeps, so the run only adds behaviours.

*Never:* a count step at any other cycle; a step of 2; a step for a sweep with an error.

*Run:* V1, with the counter's start value free (checker 3 uarch).

'''

[[tp_tbre_intr]]
==== tbre_intr: the interrupt

*Rule:* a set request for `INTR_STATE.tbre_done` comes in the cycle the engine stops being active,
and in the cycle software writes 1 to `INTR_TEST.tbre_done`; in no other cycle. `intr_tbre_done_o`
equals `INTR_STATE` and `INTR_ENABLE` both set, of the cycle the interrupt latency before, the
latency being 0 or 1 cycle and one value for the whole trace ([CIP] Event-type waveform shows an
output flop; the spec fixes the window, not the value, so the check holds for either fixed latency
and a one-cycle pulse is never lost). That `INTR_STATE` stays set until software writes 1 to it,
and that such a write wins in the cycle a sweep ends, is register file behaviour, checked in the
main testplan's xref:{tp}#tp_csr[csr].

*Observed at:* the interrupt logic's set request into the register file, the register file's
`INTR_STATE`, `INTR_ENABLE` and `INTR_TEST` outputs, `intr_tbre_done_o`.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tbre_intr_01]]`CHK_TBRE_INTR_01` |sweep end or test sets |forward |A set request in the cycle `TBRE_REGWEN` rises, and in the
cycle of an `INTR_TEST` write of 1.
|[[chk_tbre_intr_02]]`CHK_TBRE_INTR_02` |set only on end or test |backward |A set request only in such a cycle.
|[[chk_tbre_intr_03]]`CHK_TBRE_INTR_03` |line follows state |forward, backward |In every cycle, `intr_tbre_done_o` equals `INTR_STATE`
and `INTR_ENABLE` of the interrupt latency cycles before, the latency a free constant held at 0 or 1
for the whole trace. Witness: a one-cycle pulse of `INTR_STATE` and `INTR_ENABLE` with the line
never rising fails for both values. *Open point:* see Open items.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|`tbre_done` is set when a sweep ends or software tests it (`REQ_TBRE_28`) |_sweep end or test sets_ (<<chk_tbre_intr_01,CHK_TBRE_INTR_01>>)
|The check requires a set request in the cycle `TBRE_REGWEN` rises and in the cycle of a test
write. A sweep end or a test write with no set request fails it.

|`tbre_done` is set by nothing else (`REQ_TBRE_30`) |_set only on end or test_ (<<chk_tbre_intr_02,CHK_TBRE_INTR_02>>)
|A set request in any other cycle fails the check.

|The interrupt line follows the enabled state within one fixed cycle (`REQ_TBRE_31`) |_line follows state_ (<<chk_tbre_intr_03,CHK_TBRE_INTR_03>>)
|The check compares the line in every cycle with the enabled state the latency before. A line that
misses a one-cycle pulse, or stays high after the state fell, fails it.
|===

*Cases:* _end, enabled_, a sweep ends with `INTR_ENABLE` set; _end, disabled_, with it clear;
_test write_, an `INTR_TEST` write of 1; _test at end_, an `INTR_TEST` write in the cycle a sweep
ends; _end with error_, a sweep ending with an error; _line next cycle_, `intr_tbre_done_o` rising
the cycle after `INTR_STATE` and `INTR_ENABLE` are both set.

*Never:* a set request with no sweep end and no `INTR_TEST` write; `intr_tbre_done_o` high more
than the interrupt latency after `INTR_STATE` and `INTR_ENABLE` stopped being both set.

*Run:* V1.

=== Sweep

How the revocation engine works:
xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc#revocation[design architecture doc, the meta
SRAM and revocation].

.Testpoints of the sweep
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_tbre_sweep,tbre_sweep>> |A sweep reads exactly the words of the swept capabilities, full-word `Get`{empty}s with the hint and a valid integrity, at most two at a time.
|<<tp_tbre_done,tbre_done>> |Every sweep ends, given its neighbours answer.
|===

[[tp_tbre_sweep]]
==== tbre_sweep: exactly the swept words are read

*Rule:* while the engine is active, `tbre_tl_h` carries a full-word `Get` of each word of every
swept capability, at `c` and `c + 4`, and nothing else. At most two reads are outstanding, with
different `a_source`. Every read reaches the engine's tag filter with the capability-load hint.

*Observed at:* `tbre_tl_h`; the engine's tag filter's device port (the hint).

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tbre_sweep_01]]`CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_01` |sweep read carries valid integrity |forward |Every sweep read presented on the port carries a
valid command integrity.
|[[chk_tbre_sweep_02]]`CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_02` |both words read |forward |The tracked capability has both words read, a full-word `Get`
of each taken on `tbre_tl_h`, before `TBRE_REGWEN` rises.
|[[chk_tbre_sweep_03]]`CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_03` |Gets inside sweep |backward |Every request on `tbre_tl_h` is a full-word `Get` with
`BASE \<= a < BASE + 8N`, presented while the engine is active.
|[[chk_tbre_sweep_04]]`CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_04` |at most two outstanding |forward |At most two reads are outstanding on `tbre_tl_h`, and an
outstanding read's `a_source` is not reused. The second part is the TL-UL ABVIP's rule TL08 on that
port.
|[[chk_tbre_sweep_05]]`CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_05` |Gets carry hint |forward |The hint is set on every `Get` at the engine's tag filter.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Both words of every swept capability read (`REQ_TBRE_13`) |_both words read_ (<<chk_tbre_sweep_02,CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_02>>)
|The tool may choose any swept capability as the tracked one, and the check requires a taken
full-word `Get` of each of its words before the sweep ends. A skipped word fails it.

|No other request on `tbre_tl_h` (`REQ_TBRE_14`) |_Gets inside sweep_ (<<chk_tbre_sweep_03,CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_03>>)
|Every request on the port is compared with the sweep's range, kind and size. A write, a sub-word
read, a read outside the range or one while idle fails it.

|At most two reads outstanding (`REQ_TBRE_15a`) |_at most two outstanding_ (<<chk_tbre_sweep_04,CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_04>>)
|The check counts the reads taken and not yet answered. A third one fails it.

|Each outstanding read has its own `a_source` (`REQ_TBRE_15b`) |_at most two outstanding_ (<<chk_tbre_sweep_04,CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_04>>)
|The TL-UL ABVIP's rule TL08 fails a read whose `a_source` an outstanding read already uses.

|Every word read with the hint (`REQ_TBRE_16`) |_Gets carry hint_ (<<chk_tbre_sweep_05,CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_05>>)
|The check looks at every `Get` at the engine's tag filter. One without the hint fails it.

|Every sweep read has a valid integrity (`REQ_TBRE_40`) |_sweep read carries valid integrity_ (<<chk_tbre_sweep_01,CHK_TBRE_SWEEP_01>>)
|The check recomputes the command integrity of every read presented. Nothing else checks it: the
TL-UL ABVIP leaves every integrity field free.
|===

*Cases:* _across seam_, `BASE` `0x1001_FFF0`, `NUM` 4, across the seam to the second SRAM;
_clipped at top_, `BASE` `0x1002_FFF0`, `NUM` 5, clipped to `N` = 2 at the top `0x1003_0000`;
_below OTP pages_, `BASE` `0x301F_F5F8`, `NUM` 1, the last capability below the emulated OTP pages,
which read with an error; _one capability_, `N` = 1; _tracked first_, _tracked in middle_ and
_tracked last_, the tracked capability first in its sweep, in the middle and last (the same covers
as <<tp_tbre_status,tbre_status>>); _two in flight_, two reads in flight.

*Edge cases:* _last SRAM word_, the last word of the main SRAM region, `0x1002_FFFC`, read; _last
NVM word_, the last NVM word, `0x301F_FFFC`, read; _NVM top_, the end of an NVM sweep near the top,
`BASE` `0x301F_FFF0`, `NUM` 4, `N` 2. The first words past each region, `0x1003_0000` and
`0x3020_0000`, are never read: _Gets inside sweep_. A sweep of the whole NVM (`N` = `0x4_0000`) is
too long to end in a bounded run, so its end is covered with a `BASE` near the top (_NVM top_).

*Never:* a read below `BASE`, at or above `BASE + 8N`, or outside the region; a write or a sub-word
read on `tbre_tl_h`; a third outstanding read; a read while inactive; a read without the hint.

*Run:* V1. Whether a sweep continued after the top of memory is observable here: _Gets inside
sweep_ checks every request on `tbre_tl_h`.

'''

[[tp_tbre_done]]
==== tbre_done: every sweep ends

*Rule:* after a taken start, `TBRE_REGWEN` returns to 1 at some point, given `xbar_main`, the
bitmap port and the RMW filter answer.

*Observed at:* `TBRE_REGWEN`.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tbre_done_01]]`CHK_TBRE_DONE_01` |sweep ends |liveness |After a taken start, `TBRE_REGWEN` is 1 again, at some point.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Every sweep ends (`REQ_TBRE_37`) |_sweep ends_ (<<chk_tbre_done_01,CHK_TBRE_DONE_01>>)
|The tool looks for a run, with its neighbours answering, where `TBRE_REGWEN` stays 0 for ever. A
sweep that hangs gives one.
|===

*Cases:* _one-capability sweep_, a sweep of one capability ends; _sweep with clear_, a sweep with
a clear; _sweep with read error_, a sweep with a read error.

*Run:* the liveness run "3 Revocation, liveness B", with assumption A10 and contracts C1 and C2.
The engine's clears pass the real 2:1 tag arbiter, so the sweep ends only if the arbiter never
starves input 1.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for _sweep ends_: the arbiter must never starve
input 1.

=== Decision and clears

How the engine reaches the bitmap and the tags:
xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc#_how_the_tbre_uses_both_tables[design
architecture doc, how the TBRE uses both tables].

.Testpoints of the decision and clears
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_tbre_decision,tbre_decision>> |Which capabilities get a bitmap lookup and which get a clear: exactly the revoked ones no core write touched.
|<<tp_tbre_clear,tbre_clear>> |Each clear is one tag write of tag 0 to the capability's tag bit; the engine's tag filter keeps the tag filter rules.
|===

[[tp_tbre_decision]]
==== tbre_decision: which capabilities are revoked

*Rule:* for a swept capability read without error, the engine makes its lookup, of the revocation
word of its base, when it is tagged, is not a sealing capability and has a revocable base; it makes
none when the base is not revocable. It presents a clear for the capability if and only if the
capability is revoked and no core write touched it in its watch window.

*Observed at:* `tbre_tl_h` (the capability's words), the TRVK filter's downstream port (its tag,
W1's arrival), the engine's read port (W1's departure), the bitmap port, the engine's clear port.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tbre_decision_01]]`CHK_TBRE_DECISION_01` |lookup carries valid integrity |forward |Every lookup presented on the bitmap port carries a valid
command integrity.
|[[chk_tbre_decision_02]]`CHK_TBRE_DECISION_02` |lookup when needed |forward |The tracked capability, read without error, that needs a lookup
has a full-word `Get` of the revocation word of its base presented on the bitmap port while the
TRVK filter holds its W1 answer.
|[[chk_tbre_decision_03]]`CHK_TBRE_DECISION_03` |no lookup outside main SRAM |backward |No lookup is presented while the TRVK filter holds the W1
answer of a tracked capability whose base lies outside the main SRAM.
|[[chk_tbre_decision_04]]`CHK_TBRE_DECISION_04` |lookup is bitmap Get |backward |Every lookup, whatever the capability, is a full-word `Get` of
a bitmap word, `0x1100_0000 \<= a < 0x1100_0C00`, presented while the TRVK filter holds a W1 answer
that has had no lookup yet.
|[[chk_tbre_decision_05]]`CHK_TBRE_DECISION_05` |revoked gets cleared |forward |When the sweep ends, the tracked capability, read without error,
revoked and not touched in its watch window, has had its clear presented.
|[[chk_tbre_decision_06]]`CHK_TBRE_DECISION_06` |clear only if revoked |backward |Every clear presented on the engine's clear port lies in a swept
capability; for the tracked one, when it is tagged, its decision is known when the clear is
presented and is revoked. An untagged tracked capability is outside this check: the untagged rows
of the truth table have no rule.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|A capability that may be revoked is looked up (`REQ_TBRE_17`) |_lookup when needed_ (<<chk_tbre_decision_02,CHK_TBRE_DECISION_02>>), _lookup is bitmap Get_ (<<chk_tbre_decision_04,CHK_TBRE_DECISION_04>>)
|The first check requires, for any tracked capability that needs one, a full-word `Get` of its
base's revocation word in its lookup window (a DV reading, question an open question); the
second fails a lookup outside the bitmap or a second one for one W1 answer.

|No lookup for a base outside the main SRAM (`REQ_TBRE_18`) |_no lookup outside main SRAM_ (<<chk_tbre_decision_03,CHK_TBRE_DECISION_03>>), _lookup is bitmap Get_ (<<chk_tbre_decision_04,CHK_TBRE_DECISION_04>>)
|The first check fails any lookup in the window of a capability whose base is not revocable; the
second ties every lookup to a W1 answer, so none escapes the window. A DV reading (question
an open question).

|A revoked capability no core write touched is cleared (`REQ_TBRE_19`) |_revoked gets cleared_ (<<chk_tbre_decision_05,CHK_TBRE_DECISION_05>>)
|The check computes revoked from the decoded base, the permissions and the bitmap word, and
requires the clear before the sweep ends. A revoked capability left tagged fails it.

|No clear for a tagged capability that is not revoked (`REQ_TBRE_20`) |_clear only if revoked_ (<<chk_tbre_decision_06,CHK_TBRE_DECISION_06>>)
|Every clear must belong to a swept capability whose decision is revoked. A clear for a sealing
capability, a base outside the main SRAM or a clear bit fails it.

|Every lookup has a valid integrity (`REQ_TBRE_41`) |_lookup carries valid integrity_ (<<chk_tbre_decision_01,CHK_TBRE_DECISION_01>>)
|The check recomputes the command integrity of every lookup presented. Nothing else checks it: the
TL-UL ABVIP leaves every integrity field free.
|===

.Truth table: tag, sealing, base and revocation bit, with the lookup answered without error; one cover per row
[cols="1,1,1,1,2",options="header"]
|===
|Tagged |Sealing |Revocable base |Bit set |Clear

|0 |0 |0 |0 |no rule
|0 |0 |0 |1 |no rule
|0 |0 |1 |0 |no rule
|0 |0 |1 |1 |no rule
|0 |1 |0 |0 |no rule
|0 |1 |0 |1 |no rule
|0 |1 |1 |0 |no rule
|0 |1 |1 |1 |no rule
|1 |0 |0 |0 |no, and no lookup
|1 |0 |0 |1 |no, and no lookup
|1 |0 |1 |0 |no
|1 |0 |1 |1 |*yes*
|1 |1 |0 |0 |no
|1 |1 |0 |1 |no
|1 |1 |1 |0 |no
|1 |1 |1 |1 |no
|===

* Each row is one cover of the _truth table row_ family: 16 covers.
* The eight untagged rows: an untagged capability has no tag to lose; the spec neither asks for a
  clear nor forbids one, so these rows are covers only, and _clear only if revoked_ excludes them.
* Decided by: the yes row by _revoked gets cleared_; the other tagged rows by _clear only if
  revoked_, and the two rows with no lookup also by _no lookup outside main SRAM_.
* Bit set is the bit the revocation word of the base holds; where no lookup is made, rows that
  differ only in it show that the bit does not matter.
* A failed lookup turns the tagged, not sealing, revocable, bit clear row into a clear
  (<<tp_tbre_errors,tbre_errors>>).

.Cases: one parameter varied at a time
[cols="2,3,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Held |Varied |Expected clear

|bitmap word and parity |tagged, not sealing, base revocable |bitmap word `0x0000_0000`,
`0xFFFF_FFFF`, `0xAAAA_AAAA`, `0x5555_5555`, each with the base on an even bit and an odd bit: one
cover per word and bit parity |bit set
|permission set |tagged, base revocable, bit set |`p`: memory read-write, read-only, write-only,
data only; executable; sealing with only SE, only US, only U0; all three: one cover each |not
sealing
|no permissions |tagged, base revocable, bit set |`p = G 00000` (no permissions) |gap: question
an open question; proposed yes
|base at edge |tagged, not sealing, bit set |one cover per base: `0x1000_0000`, `0x1002_FFF8`,
`0x1001_FFF8`, `0x1002_0000` (main SRAM); `0x3000_0000` (NVM); `0x0FFF_FFF8`; `0x1003_0000` and
`0x1003_8000` (just above the main SRAM); `0x4000_0000` (a peripheral) |revocable base
|sealed capability |tagged, not sealing, base revocable, bit set |`otype` not 0: a sealed memory
capability |yes
|===

*Extensions, without a combinatorial explosion:*

* *Base offset in the granule:* bases `0x1000_4000` (_granule offset 0_) and `0x1000_4007`
  (_granule offset 7_) both use bit 0 of word `0x1100_0100`.
* *Base, not address:* the capability with address `0x1000_4210` and base `0x1000_41F0`
  (<<base_steps>>, worked numbers): the decision follows bit 30 of `0x1100_0104` (the base), not
  bit 2 of `0x1100_0108` (the address). _Base bit set_, base bit set with address bit clear; _base
  bit clear_, the reverse.
* *Decode corrections:* _base correction_, one cover each for `c_b = 0` and `c_b = -1`; _exponent_,
  one cover each for `E` = 0, 4, 14 and 15 (`e` = 24).
* *Where the capability is stored:* _stored in NVM_, a capability stored in the NVM with a main SRAM
  base, which is revocable.

*Never:* a lookup for a base outside the main SRAM; a lookup outside the bitmap; a clear for a
tagged capability that is not revoked (sealing, base outside the main SRAM, or bit clear); a clear
outside the sweep; a decision taken from the address instead of the base.

*Run:* V1. The testbench decodes the base and sealing from the ISA (TB architecture).

*Blocked by:* question an open question, the capability with no permissions (case _no
permissions_), which _revoked gets cleared_ and _clear only if revoked_ wait on; question
an open question, for _no lookup outside main SRAM_; question an open question, for
_lookup when needed_ and _lookup is bitmap Get_: which lookup is a capability's.

'''

[[tp_tbre_clear]]
==== tbre_clear: the clear and the engine's tag filter

*Rule:* the clear of a capability is one tag write of tag 0 to its tag word and tag bit, on input 1
of the 2:1 tag arbiter, at most one per capability per sweep. The engine's tag filter meets the
tag filter's read rules (`REQ_TF_*`) on its own ports; a write to it issues one meta request and no
host request, and is answered once, with the meta answer's error.

*Observed at:* the engine's tag filter's device, host (`tbre_tl_h`) and meta ports.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tbre_clear_01]]`CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_01` |clears tracked bit once |forward |The tracked capability's clear leaves on arbiter input 1 as a
write of tag 0 to its tag word, with its tag bit, and no second clear of it follows in the sweep.
|[[chk_tbre_clear_02]]`CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_02` |writes tag 0 |backward |Every write the engine's tag filter presents on arbiter input 1
carries tag 0.
|[[chk_tbre_clear_03]]`CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_03` |tag filter checks hold |forward, backward |The tag filter checks of checker 1
(xref:{tp1}#_tag_filter[checker 1 testplan, Tag filter]) hold on
the engine's tag filter, through the shared tag filter model with this instance's configuration: no
WTRC, tag-only writes (checker 3 uarch).
|[[chk_tbre_clear_04]]`CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_04` |write answered once |forward |A write presented at the engine's tag filter's device port makes
one meta request and no request on `tbre_tl_h`, and is answered once, `AccessAck`, with the meta
answer's `d_error`.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|A clear is one tag write of tag 0 (`REQ_TBRE_21a`) |_clears tracked bit once_ (<<chk_tbre_clear_01,CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_01>>), _writes tag 0_ (<<chk_tbre_clear_02,CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_02>>)
|The first check requires the tracked capability's clear as one write of tag 0; the second fails
any write from the engine's tag filter that carries tag 1.

|A clear addresses the capability's tag word (`REQ_TBRE_21b`) |_clears tracked bit once_ (<<chk_tbre_clear_01,CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_01>>)
|The check compares the clear's address with the tag word of the tracked capability. Another word
fails it.

|A clear names the capability's tag bit (`REQ_TBRE_21c`) |_clears tracked bit once_ (<<chk_tbre_clear_01,CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_01>>)
|The check compares the clear's bit select with the tag bit. Another bit fails it; the bit order
waits on question an open question.

|A clear goes to the arbiter's input from the engine's tag filter (`REQ_TBRE_21d`) |_clears tracked bit once_ (<<chk_tbre_clear_01,CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_01>>)
|The check looks for the clear on arbiter input 1 only. A clear on any other port fails it.

|At most one clear per capability per sweep (`REQ_TBRE_21e`) |_clears tracked bit once_ (<<chk_tbre_clear_01,CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_01>>)
|After the tracked capability's clear, a second clear of it in the same sweep fails the check.

|The engine's tag filter meets the tag filter rules for reads (`REQ_TBRE_22`) |_tag filter checks hold_ (<<chk_tbre_clear_03,CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_03>>)
|The checks of checker 1's tag filter testpoints run on this instance's ports. A read that breaks
a tag filter rule fails the same check it would on the core's tag filter.

|A write issues one meta request, the tag write (`REQ_TBRE_23a`) |_write answered once_ (<<chk_tbre_clear_04,CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_04>>)
|The check counts the meta requests of each write. None, or two, fails it. A DV reading (question an open question).

|A write issues no host request (`REQ_TBRE_23b`) |_write answered once_ (<<chk_tbre_clear_04,CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_04>>)
|Any request on `tbre_tl_h` for a write fails the check.

|A write is answered once (`REQ_TBRE_23c`) |_write answered once_ (<<chk_tbre_clear_04,CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_04>>)
|The check counts the answers to each write. A lost or a second answer fails it.

|The answer carries the tag write's error (`REQ_TBRE_23d`) |_write answered once_ (<<chk_tbre_clear_04,CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_04>>)
|The check compares the answer's `d_error` with the meta answer's. A dropped or invented error
fails it.
|===

*Cases:* _SRAM capability_, a clear of a capability stored in the main SRAM; _NVM capability_, one
stored in the NVM, for example at `0x3000_0400`, base `0x1000_4000`: clear at word `0x1100_0C10`,
bit 0; _last SRAM capability_, the last capability of the main SRAM region, word `0x1100_97FC`, bit
31; _last NVM capability_, the last NVM capability a sweep can read, `0x301F_F5F8`; _clear answer
error_, a clear answered with `d_error` (<<tp_tbre_errors,tbre_errors>>); _between reads_, a clear
answered between the two reads of the next capability (it covers `REQ_TF_11b` on this tag filter).

*Never:* a clear on `tbre_tl_h`; a second clear for one capability in one sweep; a clear writing
tag 1.

*Run:* V1.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for the tag bit of _clears tracked bit once_; question
an open question, for _write answered once_.

=== Core write watch

How the revocation engine works:
xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc#revocation[design architecture doc, the meta
SRAM and revocation]. The windows are defined in Terms (watch window, stale window, held).

.Testpoints of the core write watch
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_tbre_watch,tbre_watch>> |A capability the core writes keeps its tag: no clear after a touch in its watch window, a read instead of the clear after a touch in its stale window, and a held clear stays unchanged.
|===

[[tp_tbre_watch]]
==== tbre_watch: a capability the core writes keeps its tag

*Rule:* a touch in a capability's watch window means no clear for it. A touch in its stale window
means the RMW filter receives a read of the tag word instead of the clear. With no touch, the clear
reaches the RMW filter as a write of tag 0. A clear presented at the RMW filter stays presented,
unchanged, until accepted.

*Observed at:* `cored_tl_d` (the core's writes), the engine's read and clear ports, the 2:1 tag
arbiter's output and the RMW filter's upstream port.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tbre_watch_01]]`CHK_TBRE_WATCH_01` |clear only if untouched |backward |The tracked capability's clear is presented on the engine's
clear port only if no core write touched it in its watch window.
|[[chk_tbre_watch_02]]`CHK_TBRE_WATCH_02` |stale clear becomes read |forward |The tracked capability's clear, touched in its stale
window, reaches the RMW filter as a `Get` of the same word and bit.
|[[chk_tbre_watch_03]]`CHK_TBRE_WATCH_03` |fresh clear stays write |forward |The tracked capability's clear, not touched in its stale
window, reaches the RMW filter as the arbiter forwards it: a write of tag 0.
|[[chk_tbre_watch_04]]`CHK_TBRE_WATCH_04` |clear held unchanged |stable |Every clear at the RMW filter that is not accepted is
presented again in the next cycle, every field the same, before and after the squash.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|No clear after a touch in the watch window (`REQ_TBRE_24`) |_clear only if untouched_ (<<chk_tbre_watch_01,CHK_TBRE_WATCH_01>>)
|The check records every touch of the tracked capability from its W0 read on, and fails a clear
presented after one. Window ends at the engine's ports are a DV reading (question
an open question).

|A touch in the stale window turns the clear into a read (`REQ_TBRE_25`) |_stale clear becomes read_ (<<chk_tbre_watch_02,CHK_TBRE_WATCH_02>>)
|The check requires a `Get` of the same word and bit at the RMW filter for a clear touched in its
stale window. A clear that still arrives as a write fails it.

|With no touch, the clear stays a write of tag 0 (`REQ_TBRE_26`) |_fresh clear stays write_ (<<chk_tbre_watch_03,CHK_TBRE_WATCH_03>>)
|The check compares the request at the RMW filter with what the arbiter forwards. A clear turned
into a read with no touch fails it.

|A held clear stays presented (`REQ_TBRE_27a`) |_clear held unchanged_ (<<chk_tbre_watch_04,CHK_TBRE_WATCH_04>>)
|A clear withdrawn before it is accepted, or displaced by a core write, fails the check in the next
cycle.

|A held clear stays unchanged (`REQ_TBRE_27b`) |_clear held unchanged_ (<<chk_tbre_watch_04,CHK_TBRE_WATCH_04>>)
|The check compares every field of the held clear with the cycle before. A changed field, or a
squash applied after arrival, fails it.
|===

.Cases: what touches the capability at `0x1000_1238`
[cols="2,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Core write |Touch?

|word store to W1 |`sw` to `0x1000_123C` (W1 of the capability) |yes
|byte store |`sb` to `0x1000_123B` |yes
|capability store W0 |`csc` W0 to `0x1000_1238` |yes
|capability store W1 |`csc` W1 to `0x1000_123C` |yes
|next capability written |`sw` to `0x1000_1240`, the next capability |no: the clear proceeds
|write not yet accepted |a write presented but not yet accepted |yes
|answered inside window |a write accepted before the watch started and answered inside it |yes,
until answered
|answered before window |a write answered before the watch started |no
|===

.Cases: when the touch happens
[cols="2,5,3",options="header"]
|===
|Case |Cycle of the touch |Result

|touch with W0 read |the cycle the read of W0 is presented on the engine's read port |no clear
|touch just before clear |the last cycle before the clear is presented |no clear
|touch with clear |the cycle the clear is presented |the clear becomes a read
|touch at arrival |the cycle the clear reaches the RMW filter |held: the clear stays a write, and
the write reaches the RMW filter after it
|touch while held |while the clear is held at the RMW filter |the write reaches the RMW filter after
it
|===

*Edge cases:* _two in flight_, two capabilities in flight, the write touching one of them; _write
withdrawn_, a write presented and withdrawn before it is accepted (checker 3 has no hold assumption
on `cored_tl_d`: the spec watches "every write the core presents").

*Never:* a clear for a capability touched in its watch window; a stale clear reaching the RMW filter
as a write; a held clear displaced or changed; a clear turned into a read with no touch.

*Run:* V1; the core's tag filter is cut, its answers and meta requests bound by contracts C6 and C7.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for the windows' ends.

=== Errors

How the revocation engine works:
xref:../design_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_design_arch.adoc#revocation[design architecture doc, the meta
SRAM and revocation].

.Testpoints of the errors
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_tbre_errors,tbre_errors>> |Which errors fail a sweep (`sweep_err`) and which also raise `fatal_fault`; a read error keeps the capability, a failed lookup counts it as revoked.
|===

[[tp_tbre_errors]]
==== tbre_errors: what fails a sweep and what raises the alert

*Rule:* [ToO] Error Handling gives the engine these rows. `sweep_err` is set by nothing else. That
it stays set until software writes 1 to it is register file behaviour, checked in the main
testplan's xref:{tp}#tp_csr[csr].

[cols="4,2,1,1",options="header"]
|===
|Cause |The capability |`sweep_err` |`fatal_fault`

|`d_error` on a sweep read on `tbre_tl_h` |no clear |1 |0
|integrity fault on an answer on `tbre_tl_h` |- |1 |1
|`d_error` on the answer to a tag read or a clear |- |1 |1, from the RMW filter
|malformed answer on `tbre_tl_h` |- |1 |1
|`d_error`, integrity fault or malformed answer on a bitmap lookup |counted as revoked |1 |1
|RMW filter fault while active |- |1 |1
|===

* *An error on the answer to a tag read or a clear* comes from the meta SRAM, through the RMW
  filter: a device error on the tag path, for which the RMW filter raises `fatal_fault` ([ToO]
  Error Handling: "Device error on the tag path ... `fatal_fault` alert"). Checker 1 checks that
  alert (xref:{tp1}#tp_tag_alerts[tag_alerts]); checker 3, where
  the RMW filter is a blackbox, checks `sweep_err` for it.
* *An integrity fault or a malformed answer from the RMW filter* is no stimulus: checker 1 proves
  the RMW filter's answers well formed, and a broken meta SRAM integrity raises its own fault
  (`REQ_TAG_08`), which the RMW filter fault row turns into `sweep_err`.

*Observed at:* the answers on `tbre_tl_h`, the bitmap port and the engine's tag filter's meta port;
the RMW filter's fault inputs; the engine's set requests of `sweep_err`; the engine's fault inputs
to the alert and the alert request.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tbre_errors_01]]`CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_01` |read error, no clear |forward |A `d_error` on the answer to a read of the tracked
capability on `tbre_tl_h` means no clear for it.
|[[chk_tbre_errors_02]]`CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_02` |cause sets sweep error |forward |Each cause of the table is followed by a `sweep_err` set
request, at some point; the spec gives no bound (premise P7).
|[[chk_tbre_errors_03]]`CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_03` |error set next cycle |forward |That set request comes no later than the cycle after the
cause, so a read of `TBRE_STATUS` once the sweep has ended sees it. A DV reading (question
an open question).
|[[chk_tbre_errors_04]]`CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_04` |bad answer raises fault |forward |An integrity fault or (run V3) a malformed answer on
`tbre_tl_h`, and any failed lookup, are followed by one of the engine's fault inputs to the alert,
at some point.
|[[chk_tbre_errors_05]]`CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_05` |RMW fault raises alert |forward |An RMW filter fault input raised while the engine is active
raises the alert request in that cycle.
|[[chk_tbre_errors_06]]`CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_06` |error only for a cause |backward |A `sweep_err` set request comes only while a cause has not
had one yet.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|A sweep read error gets no clear (`REQ_TBRE_32a`) |_read error, no clear_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_01,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_01>>)
|The tool may make any capability the tracked one; a clear for it after a `d_error` on one of its
reads fails the check.

|A sweep read error sets `sweep_err` (`REQ_TBRE_32b`) |_cause sets sweep error_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_02,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_02>>), _error set next cycle_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_03,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_03>>)
|The first check looks for a run where the read error never gets its set request; the second
requires it by the next cycle (DV reading, question an open question).

|A sweep read error raises no alert (`REQ_TBRE_32c`) |`contracts` _engine faults have causes_ (contract C9), main testplan (xref:{tp}#tp_contracts[contracts]); its check ID is the main testplan's
|The contract lets the engine's fault inputs rise only for their listed causes, and a sweep read's
`d_error` is not one. A design that raised the alert for it breaks the contract.

|Any other error, integrity fault or malformed answer sets `sweep_err` (`REQ_TBRE_33a`) |_cause sets sweep error_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_02,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_02>>), _error set next cycle_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_03,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_03>>)
|Each row of the table is a cause of the first check, so a cause with no set request fails it; the
second bounds it to the next cycle. Malformed answers are reached in run V3.

|Any other error, integrity fault or malformed answer raises `fatal_fault` (`REQ_TBRE_33b`) |_bad answer raises fault_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_04,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_04>>); checker 1's `tag_alerts` _device error raises alert_ (xref:{tp1}#chk_tag_alerts_01[CHK_TAG_ALERTS_01])
|The check requires an engine fault input after a bad answer on `tbre_tl_h`; an answer that raises
none fails it. The `d_error` on a tag read or a clear raises the alert in the RMW filter, which
checker 1's check decides.

|A failed lookup counts as revoked (`REQ_TBRE_34a`) |`tbre_decision` _revoked gets cleared_ (<<chk_tbre_decision_05,CHK_TBRE_DECISION_05>>)
|Revoked includes a failed lookup, so the check requires a clear for a tagged, not sealing
capability with a revocable base whose lookup failed. A design that keeps it fails the check.

|A failed lookup sets `sweep_err` (`REQ_TBRE_34b`) |_cause sets sweep error_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_02,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_02>>), _error set next cycle_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_03,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_03>>)
|A failed lookup is a cause of the table: no set request, or a late one, fails a check.

|A failed lookup raises `fatal_fault` (`REQ_TBRE_34c`) |_bad answer raises fault_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_04,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_04>>)
|The check requires an engine fault input after any failed lookup. None fails it.

|An RMW filter fault while active sets `sweep_err` (`REQ_TBRE_35a`) |_cause sets sweep error_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_02,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_02>>), _error set next cycle_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_03,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_03>>)
|The RMW filter fault while active is a cause of the table. Which RMW filter faults count waits on
question an open question.

|An RMW filter fault while active raises `fatal_fault` (`REQ_TBRE_35b`) |_RMW fault raises alert_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_05,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_05>>)
|The check requires the alert request in the cycle the fault input rises while the engine is
active. A missed alert fails it.

|Nothing else sets `sweep_err` (`REQ_TBRE_36a`) |_error only for a cause_ (<<chk_tbre_errors_06,CHK_TBRE_ERRORS_06>>)
|Each cause gives one credit and its set request uses it up. A set request with no cause, an RMW
fault while idle included, fails the check.
|===

*Cases:* each cause alone: _sweep read error_, a sweep read's `d_error`; _host bad integrity_, a
broken integrity on `tbre_tl_h`; _tag read error_, a `d_error` on a tag read's meta answer; _clear
error_, on a clear's; _bitmap error_, a bitmap `d_error`; _RMW fault_, an RMW filter fault while
active. Then _bitmap bad integrity_, a bitmap answer with a broken integrity; _host malformed
answer_ (run V3), a malformed answer on `tbre_tl_h`; _bitmap malformed answer_ (V3), a malformed
bitmap answer; _error on first capability_, a cause on the first capability of a sweep, _error on
last capability_, on the last; _two causes at once_, two causes in one cycle; _OTP pages read_, a
read error on the emulated OTP pages (`BASE` at `0x301F_F600`, [PG]: "sweeping them results in an
error").

*Edge cases:* _RMW fault while idle_, an RMW filter fault while the engine is inactive: no
`sweep_err` set request (the alert comes from the tag path, checker 1's `tag_alerts`); _error
already set_, `sweep_err` already set by an earlier sweep.

*Never:* an alert for a sweep read's `d_error`; `sweep_err` with no cause; a failed lookup that keeps
the capability.

*Run:* V1 for errors and integrity faults; V3 for malformed answers, which the TL-UL rules of V1
exclude.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for the RMW filter faults of _cause sets sweep
error_ and _RMW fault raises alert_; question an open question, for _error set next cycle_.

[[subsystem_part]]
== Subsystem-wide and end to end

:tb: ../tb_arch/cheriot_mem_sys_tb_arch.adoc

[[terms]]
=== Terms

The rules of every testpoint read an address, a request or a response through these terms. The
checker testplans add their own terms. Values are Earl Grey's ([IF] Parameters).

==== Addresses and regions

A byte address finds its capability tag and its revocation bit from its offset in its region, the
address minus the region's base ([ToO] Metadata Encoding: one bit covers "one 8-byte capability"
or "8 heap bytes", one word "256 bytes").

[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Field of the offset |Use

|bits 2:0 |byte in the 8-byte capability: all 8 bytes share one tag and one revocation bit
|bits 7:3 |bit select inside the meta word (the tag order is question an open question; the bitmap's is given: "bit `b` of word `w` covers the eight heap bytes starting at `MainSramBaseAddr + (w * 32 + b) * 8`{empty}", [ToO])
|bits 31:8 |word index: the meta word's address is the table base plus 4 × the index
|===

[cols="2,5,4",options="header"]
|===
|Term |Meaning |Source

|Main SRAM region |From `0x1000_0000` up to `0x1003_0000`, the top excluded: the 128 KiB main SRAM
and the 64 KiB second SRAM (a finding). |[IF] `MainSramBaseAddr` (inclusive),
`MainSramTopAddr` (exclusive)
|NVM region |From `0x3000_0000` up to `0x3020_0000`, the top excluded. |[IF] `NvmBaseAddr`,
`NvmTopAddr`
|Tagged address |An address in the main SRAM region or the NVM region. |[ToO] Tag Filter: "memory
capable of holding capabilities"; [ToO] Revocation Engine: "a tagged region"
|Revocable address |An address in the main SRAM region. |[PG]: "capabilities whose base lies
outside the main SRAM region are never revoked"; [ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map: "Main SRAM
revocation bitmap"
|Region base, region top |The base and the top (excluded) of the tagged region that holds the
address. |[IF]
|Capability of an address |The address with bits 2:0 cleared: the capability that holds that byte.
|[ToO] Metadata Encoding
|Tag word |`0x1100_0000` + T + 4 × (offset / 256, rounded down), with T = `0x8C00` in the main SRAM
region and `0x0C00` in the NVM region. |[ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map; [ToO] Metadata Encoding
|Tag bit |(offset / 8, rounded down) modulo 32. |gap: an open question
|Revocation word |For a revocable address, `0x1100_0000` + 4 × ((address − `0x1000_0000`) / 256, rounded down). |[ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map, `revbm` window
|Revocation bit |((address − `0x1000_0000`) / 8, rounded down) modulo 32. |[ToO] (as above)
|===

Worked numbers, computed from the terms above (tag bits assume the order asked in an open question):

[cols="2,3,3",options="header"]
|===
|Address |Tag word, tag bit |Revocation word, revocation bit

|`0x1000_0000`, first capability of the main SRAM |`0x1100_8C00`, 0 |`0x1100_0000`, 0
|`0x1000_1238` and `0x1000_123C`, one capability |`0x1100_8C48`, 7 |-
|`0x1000_1240`, the next capability |`0x1100_8C48`, 8 |-
|`0x1000_4000` to `0x1000_4007`, one granule |- |`0x1100_0100`, 0
|`0x1000_4008` |- |`0x1100_0100`, 1
|`0x1001_FFF8`, last capability of the 128 KiB main SRAM |`0x1100_93FC`, 31 |-
|`0x1002_0000`, first capability of the second SRAM |`0x1100_9400`, 0 |-
|`0x1002_FFF8`, last capability of the region |`0x1100_97FC`, 31 |`0x1100_0BFC`, 31
|`0x3000_0000`, first NVM capability |`0x1100_0C00`, 0 |not revocable
|`0x3000_0400` |`0x1100_0C10`, 0 |not revocable
|`0x301F_FFF8`, last NVM capability |`0x1100_8BFC`, 31 |not revocable
|===

* The tables end where the next one starts: main SRAM tags at `0x1100_9800` (the meta SRAM top),
  NVM tags at `0x1100_8C00`, the bitmap at `0x1100_0C00`.
* The seam between the main SRAM and the second SRAM, at `0x1002_0000`, is inside one region: both
  sides are tagged and revocable, and their tags sit in consecutive words.

'''

==== Requests and responses

A request on `cored_tl_d` carries the tag sideband `cored_tag_h2d`; on the other ports it has
none.

[cols="2,5,4",options="header"]
|===
|Term |Meaning |Source

|CHERIoT mode |`cheriot_ena_i` is `MuBi4True` (`4'h6`). Any of the other 15 values is ePMP mode.
|[ToO] Access Checkers: "any `cheriot_ena_i` value other than a strict `MuBi4True` - including a
strict `MuBi4False`{empty}"; [HJSON] `INTERSIG.MUBI`
|`Get`, `PutFullData`, `PutPartialData` |The request's `a_opcode`. |[TLUL] opcode table
|Write |A `PutFullData` or a `PutPartialData`. |[TLUL]
|Hinted read |A `Get` with `cored_tag_h2d` set: the capability-load hint. |[CIBEX] `data_tag_o`;
[LSU]: "Also driven high on both beats of a capability load"
|Tag sideband of a write |`cored_tag_h2d` of a write: the tag to write. |[IF] `cored_tag_h2d`
|W0, W1 |A request whose address bit 2 is 0 (the lower word, the capability's address) or 1 (the upper word, its metadata). |[ToO] WTRC: "W0 at the lower and then W1 at the upper address"; [LSU]:
"low word, then high word"
|Capability store to the NVM |In CHERIoT mode, a write to the NVM region with its tag sideband set.
|[ToO] WTRC: "a write in strict CHERIoT mode to the NVM with the tag sideband set"
|Needs a lookup |In CHERIoT mode and to a tagged address, a hinted read of W0 or a write, and not a
capability store to the NVM. |[ToO] Tag Filter: "A meta lookup is needed when ..."
|Full word |`a_size` 2 at a word-aligned address. TL-UL then sets all four `a_mask` bits. |[ToO]
Access Checkers; [TLPC] `sizeMatchesMask`, `addrSizeAligned`
|Legal request on a port |In CHERIoT mode, inside the port's region, a full word, and a `Get` or a
`PutFullData`. |[ToO] Access Checkers; checker 2 requirements, Terms
|Port region |The tag port: from `0x1100_0C00` up to `0x1100_9800`, the top excluded.
`corerevbm_tl`, `revbm_tl_d` and the engine's bitmap port: from `0x1100_0000` up to `0x1100_0C00`,
the top excluded. |[ToO] Meta SRAM Address Map, "Reachable from"
|Malformed answer |An answer whose `d_opcode` is not the one its request needs (`AccessAckData` for a `Get`, `AccessAck` for a write), or whose `d_size` differs from the request's `a_size`. |[TLPC]
`respOpcode`, `d_size`: the response "must have the same size as the original request"; [HJSON]
`sweep_err`: "malformed"
|Integrity good |The response integrity and the data integrity of an answer match its fields.
|[TLUL] Usage of User Bits
|Full put |A word of a capability store that is a `PutFullData` with every `a_mask` bit set. |[ToO]
Error Handling: a partial capability store is a fault (`REQ_WTRC_10a`)
|In sequence |A W0 presented while no capability store is open, or the W1 presented as the next
capability store after its W0. |[ToO] WTRC: W0 then W1 (`REQ_WTRC_10a`)
|Faulty word |A word of a capability store that is not a full put or not in sequence, or has a bad
command or data integrity, or whose NVM answer's integrity is not good. |[ToO] Error Handling
(`REQ_WTRC_10a`)
|NVM answer good |The NVM answer of a word has no `d_error`. |[ToO] WTRC answer table
|===

* `a_source` grows at each arbiter, kept to 8 bits: the 2:1 tag arbiter shifts it left by one,
  with the input number in the lowest bit; the 4:1 arbiter shifts it left by two, with the input
  number in the two lowest bits. The answer comes back with the added bits shifted off ([TLUL]
  Source ID growth). Example: `0x15` on input 2 of the 4:1 arbiter leaves as `0x56`; the answer
  `0x56` returns to input 2 as `0x15`.
* Requesters keep the top bits of `a_source` free for that growth (assumption
  A9): one bit at the 2:1 tag arbiter, two at the 4:1 arbiter.

[[subsystem]]
=== Subsystem-wide and end to end

The alert collects causes from all three checkers, the register file is checked by the CSR
testing, and some requirements follow only from several checkers together. These testpoints close
them. The tag path's own alert testpoint, `tag_alerts`, is in the
xref:{tp1}#tp_tag_alerts[checker 1 testplan].

==== Alerts and registers

.Testpoints of the alert and the registers
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_alert_causes,alert_causes>> |The alert is requested only for a cause the Error Handling table lists, or by `ALERT_TEST`; never for a software-reachable cause.
|<<tp_alert_test,alert_test>> |A test write requests one alert until software locks the test, and the lock holds until reset.
|<<tp_csr,csr>> |Register resets, access types and the sweep register lock; the CSR integrity fault; the register file's outputs to the engine (contract C20).
|===

[[tp_alert_causes]]
===== alert_causes: the alert only for its listed causes

*Rule:* `fatal_fault` is requested if and only if one of the causes of [ToO] Error Handling that
raise it occurs, or software writes `ALERT_TEST`.

.The causes of [ToO] Error Handling, and where each is checked
[cols="5,1,3,2",options="header"]
|===
|Cause |Alert |Requirements |Testpoint

|any meta SRAM access in ePMP mode |no |`REQ_META_04`, `REQ_META_07a`-`_07c`, `REQ_ALT_04`
|`meta_refuse`
|access outside the region of the requesting port |no |`REQ_META_03`, `REQ_META_07a`-`_07c`,
`REQ_ALT_04` |`meta_refuse`
|`PutPartialData` to the meta SRAM |no |`REQ_META_06`, `REQ_META_07a`-`_07c`, `REQ_ALT_04`
|`meta_refuse`
|device error on the tag path |yes |`REQ_RMW_13`, `REQ_RMW_14`, `REQ_RMW_17`, `REQ_TAG_07`
|`rmw_errors`, `tag_alerts`
|integrity fault on a meta SRAM response |yes |`REQ_TAG_08` |`tag_alerts`
|integrity fault on the CSR interface |yes |`REQ_ALT_01` |`csr` (CSR testing)
|capability store to the NVM that does not match, or whose NVM read fails |no |`REQ_WTRC_04a`,
`REQ_WTRC_08a`, `REQ_WTRC_08b`, `REQ_WTRC_09` |`wtrc_compare`
|capability store to the NVM with a bad integrity, partial, or out of sequence |yes
|`REQ_WTRC_10a`, `REQ_WTRC_10b`, `REQ_WTRC_11` |`wtrc_faults`, bad integrity only; the rest is out
of scope (<<not_covered>>)
|any other request out of the capability store sequence |yes |`REQ_WTRC_12` |out of scope
(<<not_covered>>)
|error response to a read of the engine |no |`REQ_TBRE_32a`-`_32c` |`tbre_errors`
|any other error, or an integrity fault, on a response to the engine |yes |`REQ_TBRE_33a`,
`REQ_TBRE_33b` |`tbre_errors`
|error, integrity fault or malformed response on a bitmap lookup |yes |`REQ_TBRE_34a`-`_34c`
|`tbre_errors`
|RMW filter fault while the engine is active |yes |`REQ_TBRE_35a`, `REQ_TBRE_35b` |`tbre_errors`
|`ALERT_TEST` write |yes |`REQ_ALT_02` |`alert_test` (CSR testing)
|===

The forward direction, each cause raising the alert, is in the testpoints of the table. The
backward direction, no alert without a cause, needs the checkers together: checker 1 sees the tag
path and WTRC causes with the engine's and the register file's fault inputs free; checker 3 sees
the engine's causes with the RMW filter's, the WTRC's and the register file's fault inputs free
(the register file is a blackbox there, TB architecture D11). Each proves that its own fault inputs
rise only for their causes; two contracts on those fault signals and the CSR testing close the
argument (<<open_questions,proposed addition P2>>; checker 3 uarch D18).

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_alert_causes_01]]`CHK_ALERT_CAUSES_01` |alert only on a fault |backward |Checker 3: the
alert request is raised only in a cycle where one of the alert logic's nine fault inputs is
raised: the step from the fault inputs to the alert.
|===

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|No alert for a software-reachable error (`REQ_ALT_04`) |_alert only on a
fault_ (<<chk_alert_causes_01,CHK_ALERT_CAUSES_01>>), with `contracts` _tag path faults have causes
(contract C8)_ (<<chk_contracts_09,CHK_CONTRACTS_09>>) and _engine faults have causes (contract
C9)_ (<<chk_contracts_10,CHK_CONTRACTS_10>>) |An alert needs a raised fault input, and each fault
input rises only for its own listed causes; the three refusals of the meta access are not among
them. The two contracts are proposed (P2), so the row waits on their agreement.

|Alert only for a listed cause or `ALERT_TEST` (`REQ_ALT_05`) |_alert
only on a fault_ (<<chk_alert_causes_01,CHK_ALERT_CAUSES_01>>), with `contracts` _tag path faults
have causes (contract C8)_ (<<chk_contracts_09,CHK_CONTRACTS_09>>), _engine faults have causes
(contract C9)_ (<<chk_contracts_10,CHK_CONTRACTS_10>>) and the CSR testing (<<tp_csr>>,
<<tp_alert_test>>) |The check ties the alert to the nine fault inputs; the contracts and the CSR
testing tie each fault input to its causes. A design that raised the alert with no cause fails one
of the links. The two contracts are proposed (P2), so the row waits on their agreement.
|===

*Never:* an alert for a software-reachable cause (the five "no" rows of the cause table); an alert
with no cause.

*Run:* V1 in checkers 1 and 3; composition.

'''

[[tp_alert_test]]
===== alert_test: testing the alert, and locking the test

*Rule:* a write of 1 to `ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault` while `ALERT_TEST.regwen` is 1 requests one alert.
Once software writes 0 to `ALERT_TEST.regwen`, it reads 0 until reset (`rw0c`: a write of 1 does not
set it again) and `ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault` writes request nothing.

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|A test write requests one alert (`REQ_ALT_02`) |the common alert test; no
FPV check |It writes `ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault` and checks the alert. The register file is a blackbox
in checker 3.

|The lock reads 0 until reset (`REQ_ALT_03a`) |the common alert test; no
FPV check |It locks `regwen` at random and reads it back. It does not write 1 to `regwen` after the
lock: that case stays open until a directed test adds it.

|No test alert after the lock (`REQ_ALT_03b`) |the common alert test; no
FPV check |It expects no alert while locked. It does not test the cycle after the lock: that case
stays open until a directed test adds it.
|===

*Cases:* _test before lock_, a test write before the lock; _lock_, the lock; _test after lock_, a
test write after the lock; _regwen 1 after lock_, a write of 1 to `regwen` after the lock; _test
right after lock_, a test write in the cycle after the lock.

*Never:* a test alert after the lock; `regwen` back at 1 before reset.

*Run:* the common alert test, `run_alert_test_vseq` in `hw/dv/sv/cip_lib/seq_lib/cip_base_vseq.sv`
(imported by the sim cfg): it writes `ALERT_TEST.fatal_fault`, locks `regwen` at random, reads it
back and expects no alert while locked. The cases _regwen 1 after lock_ and _test right after lock_
stay open until a directed test adds them.

'''

[[tp_csr]]
===== csr: register behaviour and the CSR integrity fault

*Rule:* every register field resets to its value in [REGS] and behaves as its access type (`ro`,
`rw`, `wo`, `rw1c`, `rw0c`), with `TBRE_REGWEN` gating its three registers. A request on
`regs_tl_d` with a bad command or data integrity requests `fatal_fault`. The register interface
takes a request at most every other cycle. In particular: `start_err` and `sweep_err` stay set
until software writes 1; writes to `TBRE_BASE_ADDR`, `TBRE_NUM_CAPS` and `TBRE_START` have no effect
while `TBRE_REGWEN` is 0; the two registers keep what software wrote and bits 2:0 of
`TBRE_BASE_ADDR` read 0; `INTR_STATE.tbre_done` stays set until software writes 1 to it, and such a
write wins in the cycle a sweep ends.

[cols="2,1,2,3",options="header"]
|===
|Register |Offset |Reset |Access

|`INTR_STATE`, `INTR_ENABLE`, `INTR_TEST` |`0x0`, `0x4`, `0x8` |0 |`rw1c`, `rw`, `wo`
|`ALERT_TEST` |`0xc` |`0x8000_0000` |`fatal_fault` `wo`, `regwen` `rw0c`
|`TBRE_REGWEN` |`0x10` |1 |`ro`
|`TBRE_BASE_ADDR` |`0x14` |0 |`rw`, bits 31:3, gated by `TBRE_REGWEN`
|`TBRE_NUM_CAPS` |`0x18` |0 |`rw`, bits 30:0, gated by `TBRE_REGWEN`
|`TBRE_START` |`0x1c` |0 |`wo`, gated by `TBRE_REGWEN`
|`TBRE_STATUS` |`0x20` |0 |`busy` `ro`; `start_err`, `sweep_err` `rw1c`
|`TBRE_EPOCH` |`0x24` |0 |`ro`
|===

*Observed at:* `regs_tl_d`, and the register file's two sides: `reg2hw` (to the hardware) and
`hw2reg` (from it), free in the register-file unit.

A *good* request is a whole aligned word with valid command and data integrity; the checks claim
nothing for the data of any other request.

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

.Requirements
[cols="3,2,6",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|Reset values (`REQ_REG_01a`) |the generic CSR tests; no FPV check
|`csr_hw_reset` checks the reset values. The generic CSR tests cannot reach the rows hardware
drives (Run).

|Access types (`REQ_REG_01b`) |the generic CSR tests; no FPV check
|`csr_rw`, `csr_bit_bash` and `csr_aliasing` check the access types. They cannot reach the rows
hardware drives (Run).

|A request at most every other cycle (`REQ_REG_02`) |_request every other
cycle_ (<<chk_csr_15,CHK_CSR_15>>) |The check looks for two requests taken in consecutive cycles.

|CSR integrity fault raises the alert (`REQ_ALT_01`) |the generic CSR
tests; no FPV check |They add a broken command integrity and a broken data integrity on a register
write and on a read.

|`start_err` stays set (`REQ_TBRE_04b`) |the generic CSR tests; no FPV
check |They check the `rw1c` sticky bits: set until software writes 1.

|Locked base address (`REQ_TBRE_05a`) |_locked base stable_
(<<chk_csr_01,CHK_CSR_01>>) |Any change of `TBRE_BASE_ADDR` after a locked cycle fails the check,
whatever wrote it.

|Locked number of capabilities (`REQ_TBRE_05b`) |_locked num stable_
(<<chk_csr_02,CHK_CSR_02>>) |The same, for `TBRE_NUM_CAPS`.

|Locked start (`REQ_TBRE_05c`) |_locked start no strobe_
(<<chk_csr_03,CHK_CSR_03>>) |A locked write to `TBRE_START` that strobes, in its cycle or the next,
fails the check.

|Base address keeps what was written (`REQ_TBRE_06a`) |_base written_
(<<chk_csr_06,CHK_CSR_06>>), _base changes only by write_ (<<chk_csr_08,CHK_CSR_08>>), _read
returns register_ (<<chk_csr_14,CHK_CSR_14>>) |A write lands, nothing else changes the register,
and a read returns it: a lost, changed or misread value fails one of them.

|Number of capabilities keeps what was written (`REQ_TBRE_06b`) |_num
written_ (<<chk_csr_07,CHK_CSR_07>>), _num changes only by write_ (<<chk_csr_09,CHK_CSR_09>>),
_read returns register_ (<<chk_csr_14,CHK_CSR_14>>) |The same, for `TBRE_NUM_CAPS`.

|Base address bits 2:0 read 0 (`REQ_TBRE_06c`) |_read returns register_
(<<chk_csr_14,CHK_CSR_14>>) |A good read with any of bits 2:0 set fails the check.

|Interrupt state stays set (`REQ_TBRE_29a`) |_intr stays set_
(<<chk_csr_12,CHK_CSR_12>>) |A clear of `INTR_STATE.tbre_done` without a software write of 1 fails
the check.

|Software's clear wins (`REQ_TBRE_29b`) |_intr clear wins_
(<<chk_csr_13,CHK_CSR_13>>) |A write of 1 in the cycle of a set request that leaves the bit set
fails the check.

|`sweep_err` stays set (`REQ_TBRE_36b`) |the generic CSR tests; no FPV
check |They check the `rw1c` sticky bits: set until software writes 1.
|===

.Cases
[cols="2,5",options="header"]
|===
|Case |What it reaches

|write while locked |a good write to each of the three sweep registers while `TBRE_REGWEN` is 0
|write while unlocked |the same while it is 1, and a taken start
|lock seen |`TBRE_REGWEN` low then high again
|set and clear in one cycle |an `INTR_STATE` write of 1 in the cycle of a set request
|status read |a good read of `TBRE_STATUS` answered with busy set
|sticky error set and cleared |a hardware set of `start_err` or `sweep_err` in the cycle software
writes 1 to it (software's clear wins, reading an open question; covered, not asserted)
|===

The generic CSR tests add a broken command integrity and a broken data integrity on a register
write and on a read, and a write to each register.

*Never:* a start strobe while locked; a sweep register changed by anything but a write to it while
unlocked; `INTR_STATE.tbre_done` set with no set request, or cleared with no write of 1.

*Run:* two parts, both outside the three checkers (TB architecture D11). The register-file unit
(`task_RegFile_Main`, xref:{tb}#reg_file_unit[TB architecture, The register-file unit]) proves the
checks above on the real register file with everything else cut, so the hardware side is free. The
generic CSR tests (`csr_hw_reset`, `csr_rw`, `csr_bit_bash`, `csr_aliasing`, imported by the sim
cfg) check the reset values and access types and the `rw1c` sticky bits. They cannot reach the rows
hardware drives: `TBRE_START` is excluded from them ([HJSON] tag `excl:CsrAllTests:CsrExclWrite`)
and the simulation testbench runs with CHERIoT mode off, so no sweep ever starts and `TBRE_REGWEN`
is never lowered by hardware. Until `task_RegFile_Main` runs, every checker 3 result is conditional
on contract C20.

==== Mode gating, protocol and environment

.Testpoints of the protocol, the environment and the contracts
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_tlul_protocol,tlul_protocol>> |Every TL-UL port of every checker follows TL-UL, through one ABVIP instance per port.
|<<tp_environment,environment>> |Every assumption of every checker has a witness cover: the environment is not empty.
|<<tp_contracts,contracts>> |Each contract is proven in the checker that holds its logic and assumed only where the TB architecture lists it.
|===

===== Mode gating across the subsystem

*Rule:* [HJSON] `MODE_GATING`, "In ePMP mode the entire meta SRAM is inaccessible through all four
ports of the subsystem. No tag lookups are issued."; `INTERSIG.MUBI`: any `cheriot_ena_i` other than
`MuBi4True` (`4'h6`) is ePMP mode.

This is a cross-check, not a testpoint: every row is a case of the testpoint named, and each of
them covers all 16 values of `cheriot_ena_i`.

[cols="4,4,2",options="header"]
|===
|Behaviour in ePMP mode |Requirement |Testpoint

|no tag lookup for any access |`REQ_TF_04a` |`tf_lookup`
|every load answer untagged |`REQ_TF_11c` |`tf_sticky_tag`
|no capability store to the NVM: a tagged write to the NVM is a plain write |`REQ_WTRC_13a`,
`REQ_WTRC_13b` |`wtrc_store`
|every request on the four requester ports refused with an error |`REQ_META_04`, `REQ_TAG_06`
|`meta_refuse`, `tag_isolation`
|a sweep start ignored, `start_err` set |`REQ_TBRE_02a`-`_02d`, `REQ_TBRE_03` |`tbre_start`
|===

'''

[[tp_tlul_protocol]]
===== tlul_protocol: every port follows TL-UL

*Requirements:* none of its own; it checks the protocol every other testpoint relies on.

*Rule:* the TL-UL rules ([TLUL], [TLPC]) hold on every TL-UL port of a checker, through one instance
of the TL-UL assertion-based VIP (ABVIP) per port: assumed on the ports the testbench drives,
asserted on the ports the design drives; on a link between two of the design's blocks, asserted on
both ends. Asserted, for example: the answers on `cored_tl_d`, `corerevbm_tl`, `revbm_tl_d` and
`regs_tl_d`; the requests on `cored_tl_h`, `tbre_tl_h` and `meta_sram_tl`; the RMW filter's
downstream port (checker 1) and the engine's tag requests (checker 3).

*Also checked:* the answers the subsystem builds itself carry a valid response integrity: the tag
filter's merged-error answers (`REQ_TF_13a`), the WTRC's answers
(`REQ_WTRC_05e`); the access checkers' error answers
(`REQ_META_16a`, `REQ_META_16b`).

.Checks
[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]
|===
|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_tlul_protocol_01]]`CHK_TLUL_PROTOCOL_01` |TL-UL rules hold |forward and backward |Every
TL-UL rule of the ABVIP, asserted on each channel the design drives, on every port of the checker.
Checker 1: `cored_tl_d`, `cored_tl_h`, the 2:1 tag arbiter's two inputs, the RMW filter's upstream
and downstream ports. Checker 3: `tbre_tl_h`, the engine's bitmap port, the 2:1 tag arbiter's two
inputs, the RMW filter's upstream port, and the engine's four internal links (read port, TRVK
downstream port, clear port, its tag filter's device port; checker 3 uarch U53); on `cored_tl_d`
the testbench plays both ends, so the rules there are only assumed.
|===

*Covers:* the ABVIP's own covers, on every port (its uarch doc). They are generic, so a port that
can never do one, by an assumption or by the design, leaves it unreached.

*Run:* V1, every checker.

'''

*Requirements:* none of its own; it shows the environment is not empty.

*Rule:* every `assume_` of every checker has a witness cover: a trace in which the assumption holds
and the behaviour it allows happens.

[[tp_contracts]]
===== contracts: what each checker proves for the others

*Requirements:* none of its own; it checks the contracts the other checkers assume.

*Rule:* each contract of the TB architecture (xref:{tb}#contracts[Contracts]) is proven as an
assertion in the checker that holds its logic, and assumed only in the checkers listed there. Each
check proves the contract named in brackets after it.

[cols="2,3,1,6",options="header"]

|ID |Check |Kind |What it asserts

|[[chk_contracts_01]]`CHK_CONTRACTS_01` |access request accepted and answered (contract C1)
|liveness |On each access checker's requester port, every request presented is accepted unless the
requester withdraws or changes it first ([TL] §5.1, p29: a host may retract a request "by lowering
valid or modifying the control or data signals"), and while requests are accepted and unanswered,
an answer comes; given the meta SRAM accepts and answers and every requester takes its answers.
Proven in checker 2.
|[[chk_contracts_02]]`CHK_CONTRACTS_02` |RMW request accepted and answered (contract C2) |liveness
|On the RMW filter's upstream port, every request presented is accepted and every request accepted
is answered, given the access checker contract (C1). Proven in checker 1.
|[[chk_contracts_03]]`CHK_CONTRACTS_03` |engine meta request held (contract C3a) |safety |On the

|[[chk_contracts_04]]`CHK_CONTRACTS_04` |engine meta answer taken (contract C3b) |safety |The

|[[chk_contracts_05]]`CHK_CONTRACTS_05` |RMW filter takes answers (contract C4) |liveness |On the

|[[chk_contracts_08]]`CHK_CONTRACTS_08` |core meta request held (contract C7) |safety |On the

|[[chk_contracts_09]]`CHK_CONTRACTS_09` |tag path faults have causes (contract C8) |safety
|(Proposed, D15.) The RMW filter's and the WTRC's fault inputs to the alert rise only after one of

|[[chk_contracts_11]]`CHK_CONTRACTS_11` |tag port answers in order (contract C10) |safety
