Contract C20, the register file's outputs to the engine, is proven by the CSR testing
(<<tp_csr>>), not by a checker.

*Covers:* one per check, named after the precondition it reaches, in the checker that proves it: a
request waiting, an answer offered, a fault input raised; for contract C10, _tag port answer
waits_, an answer on the tag port that waits. For the order of contract C10, also _older answer
first_, an older answer taken while a later request waits, and _tracked answer last_, a request's
answer taken when no older one is left.

*Run:* in the run the TB architecture's proof order (xref:{tb}#proof_order[Proof order]) names for
each contract.

*Blocked by:* question an open question, for _core meta request held (contract C7)_
(<<chk_contracts_08,CHK_CONTRACTS_08>>), which holds only if the core holds its requests
(assumption A1).

==== End to end by composition

Each of these testpoints follows from checks the checker testplans prove, and from premises, as the
TB architecture argues (xref:{tb}#composition[End-to-end requirements by composition]). No memory
is modelled.

.Testpoints closed by composition
[cols="2,7",options="header"]
|===
|Testpoint |What it checks

|<<tp_tag_read_after_write,tag_read_after_write>> |A hinted capability load returns the tag last written to that capability; a write sets its sideband tag and changes no other tag.
|<<tp_tag_no_deadlock,tag_no_deadlock>> |Every core request is answered, whatever the engine's tag filter asks of the shared RMW filter.
|<<tp_rev_end_to_end,rev_end_to_end>> |After a clean sweep a revoked capability reads back untagged; a capability the core wrote in its watch window keeps its tag.
|===

[[tp_tag_read_after_write]]
===== tag_read_after_write: a tag reads back as written

*Rule:* a hinted capability load returns the tag most recently written to that capability through
the tag path; a write sets the tag to its sideband; a tag write changes no other tag.

*Follows from:* the checks in the table below, and assumption A11 (the meta SRAM keeps what it is given). No
memory is modelled. Closed in review once every requirement it follows from is proven.

.Requirements
[cols="3,4,5",options="header"]

|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

(xref:{tp1}#chk_arb_forward_03[CHK_ARB_FORWARD_03]), _answer to its input_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_arb_return_01[CHK_ARB_RETURN_01]), _taken with its input_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_arb_return_02[CHK_ARB_RETURN_02]), _fields unchanged_

(xref:{tp1}#chk_arb_forward_03[CHK_ARB_FORWARD_03]), _carries the updated word_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_rmw_write_back_01[CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_01]), _nothing else downstream_

(xref:{tp2}#chk_tag_isolation_03[CHK_TAG_ISOLATION_03]) |The write-back keeps every other bit of

port reaches the tag words. So no other capability's tag changes.
|===

'''

[[tp_tag_no_deadlock]]
===== tag_no_deadlock: the core is always answered

*Rule:* every core request is answered, whatever the engine's tag filter asks of the shared RMW
filter, given `xbar_main` and the meta SRAM answer.

*Follows from:* `REQ_TF_14`, `REQ_TF_15a`,
`REQ_TF_15b`, `REQ_ARB_08`,
`REQ_RMW_15a`, `REQ_RMW_15b`; contracts C1, C3b.
Closed in the liveness run (<<run_variants>>).

.Requirements
[cols="3,4,5",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|No deadlock between the two tag filters (`REQ_TAG_09`) |Checker 1:
_meta answer taken_ (xref:{tp1}#chk_tf_flow_01[CHK_TF_FLOW_01]), _request eventually accepted_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_tf_flow_03[CHK_TF_FLOW_03]), _request eventually answered_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_tf_flow_04[CHK_TF_FLOW_04]), _no starvation_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_arb_flow_03[CHK_ARB_FLOW_03]), _one answer per operation_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_rmw_single_op_03[CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_03]), _every operation answered_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_rmw_single_op_04[CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_04]). `contracts` _access request accepted and
answered (contract C1)_ (<<chk_contracts_01,CHK_CONTRACTS_01>>), _engine meta answer taken
(contract C3b)_ (<<chk_contracts_04,CHK_CONTRACTS_04>>) |The core's tag filter always takes its
meta answers, so a meta answer never waits on a data answer; the arbiter starves neither input; the
RMW filter answers every operation; the meta access accepts and answers, and the engine's tag
filter takes its meta answers. So no request of the core waits for ever.
|===

*Blocked by:* question an open question, through `REQ_ARB_08`.

'''

[[tp_rev_end_to_end]]
===== rev_end_to_end: a revoked capability loses its tag, a rewritten one keeps it

*Rule:* after a sweep with no `sweep_err`, every swept capability that was revoked when read and not
touched in its watch window reads back untagged until written again; a capability touched in its
watch window keeps the tag the core's write gave it.

*Follows from:* checker 3: the clear of a revoked capability reaches the RMW filter as a write of
tag 0 to its bit, and a touched one is never cleared or reaches it as a read (`REQ_TBRE_19`,
`REQ_TBRE_21a`-`_21e`, `REQ_TBRE_24`-`_27b`); checker 1: the arbiter forwards it unchanged
and the RMW filter writes only that bit, and writes nothing for a read (`REQ_ARB_01a`,
`REQ_ARB_01b`, `REQ_ARB_03a`-`_03f`, `REQ_ARB_04a`, `REQ_ARB_04b`, `REQ_RMW_03`, `REQ_RMW_06a`,
`REQ_RMW_06b`, `REQ_RMW_07a`-`_07c`, `REQ_RMW_16a`, `REQ_RMW_16b`); checker 2: the tag port forwards
it unchanged (`REQ_META_01a`, `REQ_META_01b`, `REQ_META_02a`-`_02g`); assumption
A11.

.Requirements
[cols="3,4,5",options="header"]
|===
|Requirement |Checked by |Why this check proves it

|A revoked capability reads back untagged (`REQ_TBRE_38`) |Checker 3:
_revoked gets cleared_ (xref:{tp3}#chk_tbre_decision_05[CHK_TBRE_DECISION_05]), _clears
tracked bit once_ (xref:{tp3}#chk_tbre_clear_01[CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_01]), _writes tag 0_
(xref:{tp3}#chk_tbre_clear_02[CHK_TBRE_CLEAR_02]), _fresh clear stays write_
(xref:{tp3}#chk_tbre_watch_03[CHK_TBRE_WATCH_03]). Checker 1:
_keeps its own sideband_ (xref:{tp1}#chk_arb_forward_01[CHK_ARB_FORWARD_01]), _from the named
input_ (xref:{tp1}#chk_arb_forward_02[CHK_ARB_FORWARD_02]), _full-word Get first_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_rmw_write_skip_01[CHK_RMW_WRITE_SKIP_01]), _answer after Get answer_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_rmw_write_skip_04[CHK_RMW_WRITE_SKIP_04]), _carries the updated word_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_rmw_write_back_01[CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_01]), _full-word Put to same word_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_rmw_write_back_02[CHK_RMW_WRITE_BACK_02]). Checker 2: _legal request forwarded_
(xref:{tp2}#chk_meta_forward_01[CHK_META_FORWARD_01]), _no extra meta SRAM request_
(xref:{tp2}#chk_meta_forward_02[CHK_META_FORWARD_02]) |The engine clears every capability revoked
when read, as a write of tag 0 to its bit that stays a write while untouched; the arbiter and the
RMW filter turn it into a write-back of that bit alone; the tag port passes it to the meta SRAM
unchanged. With the meta SRAM keeping what it is given (assumption A11), the capability reads back
untagged until written again.

|A capability the core wrote keeps its tag (`REQ_TBRE_39`) |Checker 3:
_clear only if untouched_ (xref:{tp3}#chk_tbre_watch_01[CHK_TBRE_WATCH_01]), _stale clear
becomes read_ (xref:{tp3}#chk_tbre_watch_02[CHK_TBRE_WATCH_02]), _clear held unchanged_
(xref:{tp3}#chk_tbre_watch_04[CHK_TBRE_WATCH_04]). Checker 1: _lookup in same cycle_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_tf_lookup_01[CHK_TF_LOOKUP_01]), _forwarded unchanged_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_tf_forward_01[CHK_TF_FORWARD_01]), _alone in same cycle_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_arb_flow_01[CHK_ARB_FLOW_01]), _one operation at a time_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_rmw_single_op_01[CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_01]), _nothing else downstream_
(xref:{tp1}#chk_rmw_single_op_02[CHK_RMW_SINGLE_OP_02]) |The core's write is looked up and
forwarded unchanged, passes the 2:1 tag arbiter, and the RMW filter does one operation at a time,
so its tag write lands whole. A clear the core's write overtook is not presented, or reaches the RMW
filter as a read; a clear at the RMW filter is held there. The RMW filter writes nothing for a
read, so the core's tag stays.
|===

*Run:* composition.

*Rule:* a requirement whose stimulus the main environment excludes is checked in a run without that
exclusion, never left vacuous.

[cols="1,1,4,4",options="header"]
|===
|Run |Checker |Change from the main environment |Needed by

|V1 |1, 2, 3 |none: the environments of the TB architecture |every testpoint not listed below
|V3 |3 |drop the TL-UL answer rules `respOpcode` and `d_size` ([TLPC]) on `tbre_tl_h` and the
bitmap port; the RMW filter's answers stay well formed, as checker 1 proves them |the
malformed-answer part of `REQ_TBRE_33a`, `REQ_TBRE_33b`, `REQ_TBRE_34a`-`_34c`
|V4 |3 |`cheriot_ena_i` may switch once, from any value to `MuBi4True`, while the engine is idle and
no `TBRE_START` strobe comes in that cycle (assumption A6 relaxed; TB architecture D3 (b)) |the
starts, `TBRE_REGWEN` and the epoch around a mode switch; every V1 check of checker 3
|C10 |2 |add assumption A16 on `meta_sram_tl`: answers a cycle or more after their request, in
request order, held until taken; holds only `contracts` _tag port answers in order (contract C10)_
and the environment covers (checker 2 uarch D29) |contract C10
|liveness |1, 3 |add assumption A10 and the liveness contracts, in the TB architecture's proof order
|`REQ_TF_15a`, `REQ_TF_15b`, `REQ_ARB_08`, `REQ_RMW_15a`, `REQ_TBRE_37`; `REQ_TAG_09` by
composition
|liveness A |2 |add assumption A10's first part only: the meta SRAM keeps accepting |`REQ_META_12`,
as written (checker 2 uarch D28)
|liveness B |2 |add assumption A10 in full, A10's first part, assumption A16 and contracts C4, C5
(checker 2 uarch D35) |`REQ_META_13a`; contract C1
|===

* A variant only removes restrictions, so it adds behaviours: what V1 proves stays proven, and V3
  runs only the requirements listed.
* No variant breaks the core's access order: a core that breaks it is out of scope
  (<<not_covered>>).
* Checker 3's V1 lets the epoch counter start at any value (checker 3 uarch D47): every value is one
  the counter reaches after enough sweeps, so V1 only gains behaviours, and the wrap is reachable.
* Covers run first in every variant.
* A run is not a Jasper task. Each checker has one task, `task_<Checker>_Main`, and another only
  where a check cannot share its setup (TB architecture, One environment, one task per checker). So
  V1 and liveness A share a task: a fairness assumption with no safety part changes no safety
  result.

.The Jasper task that holds each run's checks

assumes contract C3b and not contract C1 (TB architecture, Proof order)
|C10, liveness B |2 |`task_MetaAccess_MetaRspInOrder`
|V1, V3, V4, liveness |3 |not built yet
|===
